```js
// Example code here
const axios = require("axios");
const https = require("https");
const http = require("http");
const httpsAgent = new https.Agent({keepAlive: true})
const httpAgent = new http.Agent({keepAlive: true})
const url = 'https://xxxxx';
axios
  .get(url, {
    httpsAgent,
    httpAgent
  })
  .then(() => {
    console.log("success");
  })
  .catch(() => {
    console.error("error:");
  });

```
I had read the axios' code , the httpFollow and httpsFollow's options should includes customer's agent

axios use a new agent adapter the redirect url protocol

title: Error objects thrown by Axios contain the entire request including headers which can contain credentials such as API keys
body:
This is more of a FYI kind of issue.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When making a request via Axios, if an error is caught and logged as-is, it will contain the entire request object which contains headers which can include credentials such as API keys.
If someone isn't aware of this and just logs the entire error object or error.toJSON() without sanitising it, they can leak sensitive data and credentials.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A config option to not append the request object to thrown errors and keep only the standard error properties from the spec https://nodejs.org/api/errors.html#errors_class_error

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I've worked around this by creating a new error object and only copying the standard error properties and the response status to the new error and throwing that instead.

title: Identify 127.0.0.1 as localhost when processing NO_PROXY

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I am using axios in my own project cypress-ntlm-auth, and I need to support environments where corporate proxies are used. I found it very confusing that setting NO_PROXY to localhost didn't work for requests to 127.0.0.1. I had to review the axois source code to find that no such check is performed.
 
**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a comparison [close to this line](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/03e6f4bf4c1eced613cf60d59ef50b0e18b31907/lib/adapters/http.js#L125) that checks the special case when hostname is localhost or 127.0.0.1

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Setting NO_PROXY to localhost,127.0.0.1 seems a bit redundant and node supports this check natively.

**Additional context**
If the feature request is accepted I would be happy to provide the PR for it.

title: Support for React Native blob
body:
I've seen many people complaining about issues when uploading files with React Native. The best solution today is to use `fetch()` which supports the blob generated in React Native, but it lacks progress. Libs such as `rn-fetch-blob` can't be used in Expo since you'd need to eject.

Many libraries for React Native such as Firebase have upload method that has support for the React Native blob and it would be a great addition to Axios as well.

What I'd like to do is basically:

`await Axios.post(url, reactNativeBlob, ...)`

I've tried different methods with Axios, e.g. by creating FormData with the file details, such as uri, name and type, but then Axios tries to convert the file to base64 and upload it that way, which isn't what I want.

I don't know how React Native blobs are different from web blobs, but I'm really hoping that this could be supported in Axios.

title: Set name for blob upload in Edge
body:
IE Edge doesn't support the `File` constructor, so I'm having immense difficulty in being able to set the name of my blob for upload.

First I used the third parameter of the `FormData`:

```javascript
const a = new FormData();
a.append('photo', photoBlob, 'photo.png');
```

However it turns out that Edge ignores the third parameter as that simply attempts to convert the `Blob` into a `File` like so:

```javascript
const b = new File([photoBlob], 'photo.png');
```

I've tried all sorts of dubious approaches – such as assigning `name` to the `Blob` object, but no approaches change the `name` unless the object is **literally** a `File` object.

How have other people tackled this issue?

title: Confusion between `maxContentLength` and `maxBodyLength`
body:
Backgrounds,

- `axios` has a config option called `maxContentLength`, which means the max response content size.
- And `follow-redirects` provides another option called `maxBodyLength`, which means the max request body size.

I don't think they are the same. So why did we connect them in #1286?
(cc @mividtim @RubenVerborgh @emilyemorehouse)

```
if (config.maxContentLength && config.maxContentLength > -1) {
    options.maxBodyLength = config.maxContentLength;
}
```

I guess we need design a new option called `maxBodyLength` exactly and set its default value correctly to avoid cases like https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1362#issuecomment-368319644.

- If you're reporting a bug, ensure it isn't already fixed in the latest Axios version.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

**Describe the bug**
`onUploadProgress` event reports (almost) complete immediately, even though the file is clearly still uploading. I've already tried throttling the network in devtools. It's uploading to my local machine, but the browser shouldn't know that. It's a domain name that's linked to 127.0.0.1. 

Im uploading a 9MB file that takes well over 20 seconds (throttled). Immediately after uploading begins, an `onUploadProgress` reports 7MB of progress. And immediately after that, it reports the full 9MB uploaded. On the network tab, I can see the request is still uploading. It's not waiting for the server to respond or anything like that, it really is still uploading.

**To Reproduce**
Can't really give a isolated example, as you'll need a server that accepts the upload. But it goes a little something like this:

```javascript
const formData = new FormData();
const blob = new File([file.data], file.name, { type: file.type, lastModified: file.lastModified || Date.now() }); // `file.data` is an ArrayBuffer
formData.append(file.name, blob);

const config = {
  onUploadProgress: event => {
      console.log(event.loaded, event.total);
  }
};

return await axios.post('/api/postfile', formData, config);
```
We're not doing any abstraction (yet). The code literally looks like that. I've just stripped away some irrelevant parts, like where the file data is coming from. Of course, this code is wrapped in a function, hence the return statement.

**Expected behavior**
As long as the upload is truly in progress, emit `onUploadProgress` events leading from 0 up to the body size, and only emit 100% progress when the upload is truly complete.

**Environment:**
 - Axios Version 0.19.0
 - OS: Windows 10
 - Browser Firefox
 - Browser Version 72
 - Additional Library Versions: React 16.8.6, Styled-components 4.4.0, Redux 4.0.4, Redux-form 8.2.6 (and a couple more, but these are the most relevant ones)

**Additional context/Screenshots**
I've checked the changelogs, and I didn't see any fixes concerning progress events, so I'm assuming it hasn't been fixed yet.
Issue #639 handles this problem in more detail, but has been closed (but not fixed, as far as I can tell). I've tried every suggestion from that issue that applies to me.

It might help to know that it does work in Chrome. I couldn't test Edge because it doesn't have an option to throttle network.

```js
console.log(error);
console.log(error.toJSON());
console.log(error.code);
console.log(error.stack);
console.log(error.message);
console.log(error.response);
```

title: Collect common strategies to solve issues and help for pulls
body:
#### Background

Every week axios receives lots of new issues, and most of them are problems about how to get the expected response. Some of them are simple or duplicated, some are similar but with tricky differences, and some are complex without enough and clear information.

#### Possible actions

- [x] maintain a F.A.Q page or tutorial
  - something like https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1195#issuecomment-579600201, to help users try to solve the issue by themselves first
  - or better website page with interactions or something I don't know
- [x] update issue templates to collect enough information and ***reject offenders***
  - if users thought they really need to open an issue, make sure others can help them easier
  - if an issue didn't follow the template, or without potential suggestions for axios, it will be closed directly

It may be a little rude for users seeking for help. But please understand the differences between Github issues and stackoverflow questions. Issue readers are same developers like you. The best debugger is yourself, because only you know everything about the problem. You may not familiar with axios codes, but it is simple to read and easy to get familiar with.

#### About pulls

By the way, call help for more reviewers to handle the accumulated pull requests. Anyone in the community can leave comments for them. The main strategy is conservative and do not introduce bugs and too much breaking changes.

----

Everything above is my personal thoughts, which doesn't stand for axios official decisions. Forgive my non-native English, and I just wish this project can be better with the community's help.

title: More flexible ways to customize adapters
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Users may want to set different options for native `http` module, or do something with the request object. axios only supports some of them, but doesn't want to add more and more options. For example,

- #974, to set `req.setNoDelay` for http adapter
- #3498, to set `request.open(...., synchronous)` for xhr adapter
- #3422, to set `req.on('socket', cb)`
- #2233, to set `options.localAddress`
- #2498, to set `options.checkServerIdentity`
- #2930, to set `options.insecureHTTPParser`
- #3138, to set `options.dns`
- #3845, to set `options.createConnection`

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Abstract the adapter as more detailed lifecycles, like beforeSend, afterSend. I just have the basic idea, but no detailed solution.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

If only consider the options, we can add an extra config called `adapterOptions`. Otherwise, users must implement their own adapters.

**Additional context**

Should consider both xhr and http adapters to form a fixed pattern.

body:
<!-- Click "Preview" for a more readable version --

Please read and follow the instructions before submitting an issue:

- Read all our documentation, especially the [README](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/README.md). It may contain information that helps you solve your issue.

- If you're reporting a bug, ensure it isn't already fixed in the latest Axios version.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

**Describe the bug**
Large chunked responses from servers could be slow to finish when `maxContentLength` option is set.

**To Reproduce**
The following code snippet creates an http endpoint which serves huge chunked content. It then fetches the content from the endpooint with and without using `maxContentLength`. It then logs the times taken for each request to finish.

```js
const http = require('http');
const axios = require('axios').default;

const generateChunks = (chunkSize, totalChunks) => {
  let chunks = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < totalChunks; i++) {
    let chunk = ''
    for (let j = 0; j < chunkSize; j++) {
      chunk += String(j);
    }
    chunks.push(chunk);
  }
  return chunks;
}

const CHUNKS = generateChunks(5000, 1000);

const fetchChunks = (done, maxContentLength, chunksUrl = 'http://localhost:8080/chunks') => {
  const [startTime] = process.hrtime();
  axios
    .get(chunksUrl, { maxContentLength })
    .then((r) => done(`Success in ${process.hrtime()[0] - startTime} seconds.`))
    .catch(() => done(`Failure in ${process.hrtime()[0] - startTime} seconds.`))
}

const requestListener = function (req, res) {
  CHUNKS.forEach(chunk => res.write(chunk));
  res.end();
}

const server = http.createServer(requestListener);
server.listen(8080, () => {
  console.log('Running benchmarks...');
  fetchChunks((m) => {
    console.log(`withMaxContentLength => ${m}`);
    
    fetchChunks((msg) => console.log(`withoutMaxContentLength => ${msg}`), -1);
  }, 300000 * 1000);
});
```

**Expected behavior**
Fetching time for requests with and without `maxContentLength` should be about the same.

**Actual behavior**
Fetching time for requests with and without `maxContentLength` are drastically different.
```
Running benchmarks...
withMaxContentLength => Success in 10 seconds.
withoutMaxContentLength => Success in 0 seconds.
```

**Environment:**
 - Axios Version: 0.19.2
 - OS: OSX 10.14
 - Node version: 12.13.0

title: What does an axios instance do with set-cookies header ?
body:
Questions about cookies in axios have come up a lot in the past, yet, I haven't figured out yet what exactly is the behavior. And this confusion comes from a behavior that I didn't expect to happen. Let me explain.

I have an axios instance created on a mobile app that has the basic configuration to contact a server. All server APIs are routed through this only instance.
The server will serve both the mobile app, and a website. It requires authentication through a token, either from a cookie in the header or as a query param.
Upon authentication, the server responds with a "set-cookie" header containing the token. For the website, it will take advantage of browser's behavior with cookies, saving and passing cookies along with requests in future requests. In the mobile app, I manually check the "set-cookies" header, retrieve and save the token.

In all my past attempts, trying to access any server API from the mobile app, without explictly including a cookie with the token, or without explcitly including the token as a query param, failed the request with the server denying access due to missing token.

Today however, while working on some new APIs in the mobile app, I completely forgot to include the token in either place (header or query param). These new APIs however worked correctly. When I noticed, I have checked the request on the server, and indoubtly, there was a cookie with the authentication token since the initial authentication response.

In many other people's questions, it is always mentioned that axios will not pass cookies further automatically the same way a browser would - yet, here I am making requests through an axios instance that, it seems, passes cookies along just fine.

So now I am wondering, what is the behavior of axios with cookies?
Is the behavior I experienced specific to an axios instance only?
Does axios discard them after presenting the server response (resolving the promise)?
Does axios pass the cookies along in future requests?
Can I rely on an axios instance passing cookies along in it's requests?

p.s. with "axios instance" I mean an object returned by `axios.create({ ... });`

title: Connection Timings: dns, tcp, tls, firstByte...
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
So, I'm instrumenting some clients for distributed tracing using jaeger and I'm very frustrated that there's no way (at least I don't know :cry:) to get request timings statistics from axios, like: `dnsLookup`, `tcp`, `tls`, ...

Some other clients implement this feature, like `request` (now deprecated) and [`got`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/got#timings).

I think these statistics may be very valuable when trying to find bottlenecks in a distributed context. Is there a plan to implement this on the roadmap? :pray: 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
`got` implements a solution that seems good enough for me - in the response object there will be a `timings` object (https://github.com/sindresorhus/got#timings):
```
- start - Time when the request started.
- socket - Time when a socket was assigned to the request.
- lookup - Time when the DNS lookup finished.
- connect - Time when the socket successfully connected.
- secureConnect - Time when the socket securely connected.
- upload - Time when the request finished uploading.
- response - Time when the request fired response event.
- end - Time when the response fired end event.
- error - Time when the request fired error event.
- abort - Time when the request fired abort event.
- phases
  - wait - timings.socket - timings.start
  - dns - timings.lookup - timings.socket
  - tcp - timings.connect - timings.lookup
  - tls - timings.secureConnect - timings.connect
  - request - timings.upload - (timings.secureConnect || timings.connect)
  - firstByte - timings.response - timings.upload
  - download - timings.end - timings.response
  - total - (timings.end || timings.error || timings.abort) - timings.start
```

title: Caseless header comparison in the HTTP adapter
body:
**Describe the bug**
The HTTP adapter does not use caseless comparison before overriding the `User-Agent` header or deleting the `Authorization` header.

It also overwrites any provided `Content-Length` header.

**To Reproduce**
```js
axios({
  method: 'post',
  url: 'https://postman-echo.com/post',
  auth: {
    username: 'janedoe',
    password: 's00pers3cret'
  },
  headers: {
    authorization: 'foo',
    'Content-Length': 10,
    'User-agent': 'bar'
  },
  data: {
    firstName: 'Fred',
    lastName: 'Flintstone'
  }
})  
.then(function (response) {
  console.log(response.data);
})
.catch(function (error) {
  console.log(error);
});


> { args: {},
  data: { firstName: 'Fred', lastName: 'Flintstone' },
  files: {},
  form: {},
  headers:
   { 'x-forwarded-proto': 'https',
     host: 'postman-echo.com',
     'content-length': '44',
     accept: 'application/json, text/plain, */*',
     authorization: 'foo',
     'content-type': 'application/json;charset=utf-8',
     'user-agent': 'axios/0.18.1',
     'x-forwarded-port': '443' },
  json: { firstName: 'Fred', lastName: 'Flintstone' },
  url: 'https://postman-echo.com/post' }
```

**Expected behavior**
The server should have received the following headers

```js
     'x-forwarded-proto': 'https',
     host: 'postman-echo.com',
     'content-length': '10', // not '44'
     accept: 'application/json, text/plain, */*',
     authorization: 'Basic amFuZWRvZTpzMDBwZXJzM2NyZXQ=', // not 'foo'
     'content-type': 'application/json;charset=utf-8',
     'user-agent': 'bar', // not 'axios/0.18.1'
     'x-forwarded-port': '443'
```

I have a PR ready, but saw you prefer an issue be created first.

**Description**
When calling the `toJSON` method on an axios error (inside a `catch` clause), the returned object does not include the error status code. 
`toJSON` is useful for extracting the main error details, and the status code should be part of it as well.

**To Reproduce**
Run the below code. No status code field in the output. 
The only place status code appears in the `toJSON` object is in the message: "Request failed with status code **404**"

There's a `status` field (which is always `undefined` btw), but according to the code, it is a connection error string (for example, 'ECONNABORTED'), not the response numeric status code.

```js
const axios = require('axios');

axios.get('http://google.com/404')
  .catch(function (error) {
    console.log(error.toJSON());
  })
```

**Expected behavior**
A numeric `statusCode` field should be part of the `toJSON` returned object.

title: CancelToken causes memory leak if re-used for multiple requests
body:
Obtaining a cancel token (as per the Axios documentation on github) and re-using it across many requests results in a major memory leak as the payload for each request is not freed.

I am transferring large files - from 3 GB to 100GB using a chunked protocol and 20MB requests. The memory fills and remains until the cancel token reference is removed. Using the same code but not setting the cancel token in the config resolved the issue.

Creating a cancel token for each and every single request individually and removing the reference to the cancel token achieves the expected behaviour and frees the request payload memory.

Simple use of chrome dev tools and memory profile shows the cancel token as holding the memory, also reflect in process stats using top.

This is not using the global axios but an instance.

Previously reported in #1118 but it is unclear if this was properly resolved. 

Axios 0.19.2
OS Linux
Browsers: Firefox 76.0, Opera 68.0.3618.63, Chromium 81.0.4044.129

title: Why does Axios not encode all reserved characters?
body:
<!-- Click "Preview" for a more readable version --

Please read and follow the instructions before submitting an issue:

- Read all our documentation, especially the [README](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/README.md). It may contain information that helps you solve your issue.
- Ensure your issue isn't already [reported](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue).
- If you aren't sure that the issue is caused by Axios or you just need help, please use [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/axios) or [our chat](https://gitter.im/mzabriskie/axios).
- If you're reporting a bug, ensure it isn't already fixed in the latest Axios version.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

Seems that Axios is using encodeURIComponent, then undoing some of its effects by doing character replacement on a set of reserved characters (according to RFC3986). In our case this caused some unexpected failures as a network load balancer was rejecting URL's with queries that contained what it considered any 'unsafe' characters, in this case a $ sign. What is the logic behind undoing the encoding of these reserved characters? Seems that it would be safer to just let encodeURIComponent do its thing and trust the browser vendor to keep up with the RFC! Better to encode any reserved characters I think since any server will decode any % encoding regardless. It might be rare case that an un-encoded $ sign for example will cause failures, but we ran into one and I'll bet there are others out there.


In /lib/helpers/buildURL.js:

```js
function encode(val) {
  return encodeURIComponent(val).
    replace(/%3A/gi, ':').
    replace(/%24/g, '$').
    replace(/%2C/gi, ',').
    replace(/%20/g, '+').
    replace(/%5B/gi, '[').
    replace(/%5D/gi, ']');
}

```

title: Add a 3-parameter get request (url, body, config)
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...]
http methods (including Get) allow a body, and this is quite commonly used in JSON APIs.
axios client.post, etc have 3 parameters (url, body, config).
However, client.get only has two parameters (url, config).
This is in principle not a big problem because you can pass the body in the config.
However, since javascript ignores extra parameters, a call
client.get (url, body, config) will not have an error, but the body will be used as config, ignoring the real config.
It is easy to make a mistake if you are an axios beginner.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
I would like client.get to accept also three arguments for consistency with post, etc, while keeping the old 2-parameter functionality for compatibility and common usage.

body:
<!-- Click "Preview" for a more readable version --

If you found an area that needs clarification, feel free to open a PR or list the section/content that could be improved below

Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to refer to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->
in[Request Config](https://github.com/axios/axios#request-config),it says

>   responseType: 'json', // default

But after read the code 
[XMLlHttpRequest parse result ](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/adapters/xhr.js#L59)
[parse the response ](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/defaults.js#L61)

and by Testing, when you do not explicitly declaration **responseType: 'json'**，and the Http response is unqualified JSON format, Axios  use **JSON.parse ** to parse the response string , the code cach the exception but not reject the error, in the end , you get a string neither an object  nor an null object. 


So I suggest the doc Should explicitly tell the users, the config **responseType: 'json'** is not default and when the response is unqualified JSON format data, you will get an string not an expected object.

- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Sometimes (in Node.js) I want to
1. Encrypt the entire body of a request before I send it ([using a `Cipher` object](https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#crypto_class_cipher))
2. Recieve HTTP responses which contain encrypted data which I want decrypted ([using a `Decipher` object](https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#crypto_class_decipher))

while making use of Axios features such as the ability to control `responseType` as well as `interceptors`.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
There are two new options in the `RequestConfig`:
* `Cipher`: [a `Cipher` object](https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#crypto_class_cipher) which if supplied will be used to encrypt the data in the request body before/as it is sent.
* `Decipher`: [a `Decipher` object](https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#crypto_class_decipher) which if supplied will be used to decrypt the data in the response body before it is provided back to user code.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
* Using request/response interceptors to provide this encryption/decryption at that level.

The big problem with this approach is that request interceptors are applied before the response is converted to a byte array that can be encripted. Thus the code to apply encryption to a stream request vs an object request is quite different.  It would be easier if this transformation could be applied closer to the underlying `http` call. The inverse applies to response interceptors.

Additionally, this functionality is quite generic and so it might be beneficial to multiple people if this was included as a library feature.

*None*

title: Protocol not parsed when setting proxy config from env vars
body:
When setting proxy config from env vars, the proxy config protocol is not set based on the env var URL which means it always tries to the proxy server using HTTP.  If you set HTTPS_PROXY to an HTTPS URL...

```bash
export HTTPS_PROXY=https://localhost:8080
```

then the proxy config will be set without `protocol`,  which is used later on to initiate the proxy connection.

```javascript
proxy: {
  host: 'localhost'
  port: 8080
}
```

The proxy config should include protocol when parsing from env vars.

```javascript
proxy: {
  host: 'localhost'
  port: 8080,
  protocol: 'https'
}
```

To reproduce this issue, create a local HTTPS proxy with mitmproxy and set `HTTPS_PROXY` to `https://localhost:8080`. mitmproxy will respond with a 400 and the error message `HTTP protocol error in client request: Invalid request scheme: https`.

-->

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Use "axios.use", not an interceptor, it's middleware runs as an onion model.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
like a koa middleware.
```javascript
axios.use(async (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.config.headers = xxx
  await next();
  ctx.config.data = xxx
});
```

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
No

#### Additional context
compose.js
```javascript
'use strict';

var utils = require('../utils');

/**
 * Expose compositor.
 * form https://github.com/koajs/compose/blob/master/index.js
 */

/**
 * Compose `middleware` returning
 * a fully valid middleware comprised
 * of all those which are passed.
 *
 * @param {Array} middleware
 * @return {Function}
 * @api public
 */

function compose(middleware) {
  if (!Array.isArray(middleware)) {throw new TypeError('Middleware stack must be an array!');}
  utils.forEach(middleware, function forEachMiddlewareNotFunction(fn) {
    if (typeof fn !== 'function') {throw new TypeError('Middleware must be composed of functions!');}
  });

  /**
   * @param {Object} context
   * @return {Promise}
   * @api public
   */

  return function callMiddleware(config, next) {
    // last called middleware #
    var index = -1;
    function dispatch(i) {
      if (i <= index) {return Promise.reject(new Error('next() called multiple times'));}
      index = i;
      var fn = middleware[i];
      if (i === middleware.length) fn = next;
      if (!fn) return Promise.resolve();
      try {
        return Promise.resolve(fn(config, dispatch.bind(null, i + 1)));
      } catch (err) {
        return Promise.reject(err);
      }
    }
    return dispatch(0);
  };
}

module.exports = compose;
```
Axios.js
```javascript
// use middleware
Axios.prototype.use =  function use(fn) {
  if (typeof fn !== 'function') throw new TypeError('middleware must be a function!');
  this.middleware.push(fn);
  return this;
};


/**
 * Dispatch a request
 *
 * @param {Object} config The config specific for this request (merged with this.defaults)
 */
Axios.prototype.request = function request(config) {
  /*eslint no-param-reassign:0*/
  // Allow for axios('example/url'[, config]) a la fetch API
  if (typeof config === 'string') {
    config = arguments[1] || {};
    config.url = arguments[0];
  } else {
    config = config || {};
  }

  config = mergeConfig(this.defaults, config);

  // Set config.method
  if (config.method) {
    config.method = config.method.toLowerCase();
  } else if (this.defaults.method) {
    config.method = this.defaults.method.toLowerCase();
  } else {
    config.method = 'get';
  }

  // middleware
  var isMiddleware = config.middleware;
  if (isMiddleware) {
    var fnMiddleware = compose(this.middleware.concat(dispatchRequest));
    return fnMiddleware(config);
  }

  // Hook up interceptors middleware
  var chain = [dispatchRequest, undefined];
  var promise = Promise.resolve(config);

  this.interceptors.request.forEach(function unshiftRequestInterceptors(interceptor) {
    chain.unshift(interceptor.fulfilled, interceptor.rejected);
  });

  this.interceptors.response.forEach(function pushResponseInterceptors(interceptor) {
    chain.push(interceptor.fulfilled, interceptor.rejected);
  });

  while (chain.length) {
    promise = promise.then(chain.shift(), chain.shift());
  }

  return promise;
};
```

-->

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I'm currently using Axios as an external tool (ran from shell) to test some of my APIs. Most of them use cookies and Axios doesn't support cookies outside standard browser env

#### Describe the solution you'd like
The same as if it was running in standard browser env

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
Just create a local in-memory store. Here is the code I made for:

**/lib/helpers/cookies.js**

```
'use strict';

var utils = require('./../utils');
const localStore = {};

module.exports = (
  utils.isStandardBrowserEnv() ?

  // Standard browser envs support document.cookie
    (function standardBrowserEnv() {
      return {
        write: function write(name, value, expires, path, domain, secure) {
          var cookie = [];
          cookie.push(name + '=' + encodeURIComponent(value));

          if (utils.isNumber(expires)) {
            cookie.push('expires=' + new Date(expires).toGMTString());
          }

          if (utils.isString(path)) {
            cookie.push('path=' + path);
          }

          if (utils.isString(domain)) {
            cookie.push('domain=' + domain);
          }

          if (secure === true) {
            cookie.push('secure');
          }

          document.cookie = cookie.join('; ');
        },

        read: function read(name) {
          var match = document.cookie.match(new RegExp('(^|;\\s*)(' + name + ')=([^;]*)'));
          return (match ? decodeURIComponent(match[3]) : null);
        },

        remove: function remove(name) {
          this.write(name, '', Date.now() - 86400000);
        }
      };
    })() :

  // Non standard browser env (web workers, react-native) lack needed support.
    (function nonStandardBrowserEnv() {
      return {
        write: function write(name, value, expires, path, domain, secure) {
          const cookie = [];

          if (utils.isNumber(expires)) {
            cookie.push('expires=' + new Date(expires).toGMTString());
          }

          if (utils.isString(path)) {
            cookie.push('path=' + path);
          }

          if (utils.isString(domain)) {
            cookie.push('domain=' + domain);
          }

          if (secure === true) {
            cookie.push('secure');
          }

          localStore[name] = cookie.join('; ');
        },
        read: function read(name) {
          return localStore[name] ? localStore[name] : null;
        },
        remove: function remove() {
            delete localStore[name];
        }
      };
    })()
);
```

#### Additional context
For those that are stuck with this problem, the only work-around I found is by using interceptors, here is a sample:
```
const cookieInterceptor = requester.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
	config.headers['cookie'] = `connect.sid=${cookie.value};`;
	return config;
});
```

```js
axios.defaults.headers.common['content-type'] = 'application/json';
```

This request header Content-Type become  `application/json, application/json;charset=utf-8`.  
GET / POST methods option can use `'content-type'` too. 
But `defaults.headers` is only allow the `'Content-Type'` ?  

#### Example Code

Global axios defaults
```js
axios.defaults.headers.common['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';
// Request Header Content-Type: application/json

axios.defaults.headers.common['content-type'] = 'application/json';
// Request Header Content-Type: application/json, application/json;charset=utf-8

axios.defaults.headers.common['Content-type'] = 'application/json';
// Request Header Content-Type: application/json, application/json;charset=utf-8
```

Request methods config
```js
axios.get(url, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });
// Request Header Content-Type: application/json

axios.get(url, { headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } });
// Request Header Content-Type: application/json

axios.get(url, { headers: { 'Content-type': 'application/json' } });
// Request Header Content-Type: application/json

axios.get(url, { headers: { 'cOntEnt-tYpe': 'application/json' } });
// Request Header Content-Type: application/json
```

Content-Type `application/json, application/json;charset=utf-8` requests ite become empty `req.body` in Express.

```js
// Express API
const express = require('express');
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());

app.post('/api', (req, res) => {
  // Always `req.body` become `{}` 
  // When Content-Type is "application/json, application/json;charset=utf-8"
  req.body;
});
```

#### Expected behavior, if applicable

Request methods config can use `Content-Type` and `content-type` too. (This document was written the `"content-type"` in [Response Schema](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/README.md#response-schema) )
But `defaults.headers` can use only `Content-Type`.
It's made me little confused. I sorry, I don't know if it's a specification or not.  
if it's a specification, need a note of this on the "[Global axios defaults](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/README.md#global-axios-defaults)" section, I think. Thank you.

- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the bug
The documentation states this:

```
  // `responseType` indicates the type of data that the server will respond with
  // options are: 'arraybuffer', 'document', 'json', 'text', 'stream'
  //   browser only: 'blob'
  responseType: 'json', // default
```

However, the `responseType` of `XMLHttpRequest` is left unset (same as `"text"`) by default instead of being set set to `'json'`. This causes an empty response body to become `""` instead of `null` as expected from the [XMLHttpRequest specification](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#json-response) :

> A **JSON response** is the return value of these steps:
> 1. **If response’s body is null, then return null.**
> 2. Let jsonObject be the result of running parse JSON from bytes on received bytes. If that threw an exception, then return null.
> 3. Set response object to jsonObject and return it.
>
> A **text response** is the return value of these steps:
> 1. **If response’s body is null, then return the empty string.**

#### To Reproduce
Create a request with the XHR adapter where the server responds with an empty body. Then `response.data === ""`.

#### Expected behavior
`request.responseType` should be set to `'json'` or the documentation updated.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version: 0.19.2
 - Adapter: XHR
 - Browser: Chrome
 - Browser Version: 83
 - OS: Windows 10

author: kiprobinson

title: Give axios.delete() a data parameter (similar to put/post)
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
The backend I'm working with requires a user to provide a reason for deleting a record, which is stored for auditing. The `deleteReason` comes in a body parameter. For put/post methods, this would be passed in the `data` parameter. But `axios.delete` method does not take an optional `data` parameter like the `put` and `post` methods.

```
axios.delete(url[, config])
axios.post(url[, data[, config]])
axios.put(url[, data[, config]])
```

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I'd like the delete method to be defined similar to put/post:

```
axios.delete(url[, data[, config]])
axios.post(url[, data[, config]])
axios.put(url[, data[, config]])
```

So that I could do this:

```
let deleteDocument = axios.delete('/whatever', { deleteReason: "This doc is bad" });
```

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
I know there are two workarounds, but those don't follow the same pattern as axios.put and axios.post:

```
let deleteDocument = axios.delete('/whatever', { data: { deleteReason: "This doc is bad" } });
let deleteDocument = axios({method: 'delete', url: '/whatever', { data: { deleteReason: "This doc is bad" } });
```

#### Section/Content To Improve

Quote: "For convenience aliases have been provided for all supported request methods."

#### Suggested Improvement

The key word in the quote is "supported". This suggests to me that anything not listed is not supported. `search` is not in the list, which implies that the SEARCH method is not supported. However, I tried the following:

```
axios.request({

});
```

-->

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

N/A

#### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like Hooks to be added to Axios. Hooks allow modifications during the request lifecycle. Hook functions are run serially. Having the ability to asign hook to different event that occurs in the request lifecycle.

Events like:

1. beforeRequest
1. afterResponse
1. beforeError

So that we could do this:

###### beforeRequest Hooks

Type: `Function[]`\
Default: `[]`

The beforeRequest Hooks are trigered before the request is made.

```js
const axios = require("axios");

axios({
  method: "get",
  url: "http://localhost:3000/",
  token: "JWT irierijeriheirheirhierh",
  // Hooks
  hooks: {
    // the beforeRequest hook is executed befor the network call is made
    beforeRequest: [
      /**
       * this a beforeRequest hook
       * @param {function} next this is the refrence to the next hook
       * @param {*} options this is the request config passed to axios
       */
      (next, options) => {
        //option is the request config passed to axios
        if (!options.token) {
          next(new Error("Token required"));
          return;
        }
        options.headers = {};
        options.headers["Authorization"] = options.token;
        console.log("pre1");
        next({msg: 'message from pre1'});
      },
      function (next, arg) {  //value is the value passed from the previous pre hook
        console.log("pre2");
        next();
      },
    ],
    // this is the error handler that handles any error passed to the next function
    errorHandler: (err) => {
      console.error("this is the error from hook:", err);
    },
  },
})
  .then(function (response) {
    console.log(response.data);
  })
  .catch((err) => {
    console.log(err);
  });
```

###### afterResponse Hooks

Type: `Function[]`\
Default: `[]`

**Note:** When using streams, this hook is ignored.

The afterResponse Hooks are trigered after the request is made.

```js
const axios = require("axios");

axios({
  method: "get",
  url: "http://localhost:3000/",
  // Hooks
  hooks: {
    // the afterResponse hook is executed after the network call is made
    afterResponse: [
      /**
       * this a afterResponse hook
       * @param {function} next this is the refrence to the next hook
       * @param {*} response this is the response gotten from the network call
       * @param {function} retryWithMergedOptions this is the retry request function.
       */
      (next, response, retryWithNewConfig) => {
        if (response.statusCode === 401) {
          // Unauthorized
          const updatedConfig = {
            headers: {
              token: user.refreshToken(), // Refresh the access token
            },
          };
          // Make a new retry
          retryWithNewConfig(updatedConfig);
        }
        console.log("post1");
        // No changes otherwise
        next();
      },
    ],
    // this is the error handler that handles any error passed to the next function
    errorHandler: (err) => {
      console.error("this is the error from hook:", err);
    },
  },
})
  .then(function (response) {
    console.log("fn() => ", response.data);
  })
  .catch((err) => {
    console.log(err);
  });
```

###### beforeError Hooks

Type: `Function[]`\
Default: `[]`

**Note:** error passed to the next fucntion in the beforeError hooks is throw in the catch block of the axios function call.

```js
const axios = require("axios");

axios({
  method: "get",
  url: "http://localhost:3000/",
  // Hooks
  hooks: {
    // the beforeError hook is executed after an error
    beforeError: [
      /**
       * this a beforeError hook
       * @param {function} next this is the refrence to the next hook
       * @param {*} error this is the error gotten from the network call or thrown in the pre Hooks
       */
      (next, error) => {
        const { response } = error;
        if (response && response.body) {
          error.name = "GitHubError";
          error.message = `${response.body.message} (${response.statusCode})`;
        }
        next(error);  // this is passed to the catch block of the axios function call
      },
    ],
    // this is the error handler that handles any error passed to the next function
    errorHandler: (err) => {
      console.error("this is the error from hook:", err);
    },
  },
})
  .then(function (response) {
    console.log(response.data);
  })
  .catch((err) => {
   // err is the Error passed from the beforError hook
    console.log(err);
  });
```

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

N/A

N/A

title: Is there a callback to retrieve response headers before the body?
body:
#### Describe the issue
Hello team,
we use axios to talk to multiple services and faced an interesting issues related to the timeout usage. E.g. when we send a request to the server with keepAlive set to `true` and the `timeout` set to 60 seconds then axios would wait for 60 seconds for a response with an empty body that does not contain the Content-Length header. Exactly the same situation is observed with curl:

```
curl -v -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8200/wd/hub/session/8b606843-a868-4b6a-a604-edfe5cca0317/frame
* Trying 127.0.0.1...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 8200 (#1)
> GET /wd/hub/session/8b606843-a868-4b6a-a604-edfe5cca0317/frame HTTP/1.1
> Host: 127.0.0.1:8200
> User-Agent: curl/7.55.1
> Accept: /
>
< HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
< Connection: keep-alive
< Pragma: no-cache
< Cache-Control: no-store
< Content-Encoding: identity
* no chunk, no close, no size. Assume close to signal end
```

#### Example Code


```js
let requestConfig = {
      url,
      method,
      headers: {
        'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
        'user-agent': 'appium',
        accept: 'application/json, */*',
      },
      proxy: false,
      httpAgent: this.httpAgent,
      httpsAgent: this.httpsAgent,
      cancelToken: this._reqCancelSource.token,
      keepAlive: true,
      maxSockets: 30,
      maxFreeSockets: 10,
      timeout: 60000,
};
await axios(requestConfig);
```

#### Expected behaviour, if applicable
I understand the current behaviour and accept it. My question is, however, whether a workaround is possible to fetch response headers (maybe in a callback) as soon as these headers are received by axios (and response body retrieval is still in progress) and cancel/stop the request? We'd like to detect the missing `Content-Length` header to avoid the unnecessary delay without touching the server code.
Thanks for your help in advance.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.20.0
 - Adapter HTTP
 - Browser -
 - Browser Version -
 - Node.js Version 12.8.0
 - OS: OSX 10.15.5
 - Additional Library Versions -

body:

Please read and follow the instructions before submitting an issue:

- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the bug
There is an ongoing issue with axios messing around with the 'Content-Type' headers and deleting or changing them based on its interpretation of what data type is being sent. This has caused widespread confusion and at least a dozen bug reports.

This is especially annoying when axios is being used on a server to call to another server.

#### To Reproduce
This code is running on a server. When a document is requested, it checks whether the server response indicates that it's a protected page and then attempts to log in by using a POST call with a urlencoded string as data and the Content-Type set accordingly. Axios deletes the Content-Type header, which causes the login to fail.

```
	async _get(url) {
		let resp;
		if (url.split('://')[0] !== 'https') {
			url = this.baseURL + url;
		}

		try {
			resp = await this.axios.get(url, this.config);
			if (resp.headers['x-com-ibm-team-repository-web-auth-msg'] === 'authrequired') {
				console.log('Authenticating via Form based auth...');
				const authUrl = this.baseURL + resp.headers['set-cookie'][0].match(/Path=\/([^;]+)/)[1] + '/j_security_check';
				const data = '' + querystring.stringify({
					j_username: this.username,
					j_password: this.password
				});

				const config = {
					url: authUrl,
					method: 'post',
					data: data,
					headers: {
						'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=utf-8',
						'x-test': 'something',
					}
				};
				console.log(config);
				
				try {
					resp = await this.axios(config);
				} catch (e) {
					console.log('Form based authentication failed');
					console.log(e);
					return null;
				}
			}
		} catch (e) {
			console.log('Request failed, url = ', url);
			console.log(e);
			return null;
		}
		printResp(resp);		
		return xml2js.parseStringPromise(resp.data);
	};
```


#### Expected behavior
If the Content-Type header has been explicitly set in the config then it should be left that way. If you must, generate a warning or something but axios should assume that the user has set it for a reason if it's in the custom headers of a config and accept the override.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version: 0.19.2
 - Adapter: default
 - Node.js Version: 12.18.3
 - OS: Win10

#### Additional context/Screenshots
This is the console log from the code above. You can clearly see the custom header, and the string data in the config, but then that's been overridden in the actual POST, which then causes the remote server to send back a login page, which the XML parser chokes on.


title: #1773 deletes content-type header set by developer.
body:
I have a chunked file uploader, all data is to be sent as application/octet-stream in PUT in a binary stream.
This worked in 0.19.2.

However, 0.20.0 fails because of code added under  #1773 "Fixing overwrite Blob/File type as Content-Type in browser.".

Line 21 lib/adapters/xhr.js:

```
    if (
      (utils.isBlob(requestData) || utils.isFile(requestData)) &&
      requestData.type
    ) {
      delete requestHeaders['Content-Type']; // Let the browser set it
    }

```

This "fix" now breaks my application as it assumes the browser knows best - it doesn't. It also is semantically inaccurate to set the content type to something like image/jpeg when the data is 20MB chunk from the middle of a  jpeg file - the data is NOT of content type image/jpeg.

The "fix" applied in #1773 appears to be fixing overwrite caused by setting of default content-type headers but this solution removes ANY control over the header by the developer.

Axios should NOT delete the content type header set by the developer specifically on the request. The power to control this should remain with the calling code and not be dictated by the library.

body:
<!-- Click "Preview" for a more readable version --

If you found an area that needs clarification, feel free to open a PR or list the section/content that could be improved below

Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to refer to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Section/Content To Improve

https://github.com/axios/axios#request-config

>  // `headers` are custom headers to be sent
>  headers: {'X-Requested-With': 'XMLHttpRequest'},


>   // `data` is the data to be sent as the request body
>  // Only applicable for request methods 'PUT', 'POST', 'DELETE , and 'PATCH'


#### Suggested Improvement

The documentation should be clearer on the magic behind the suppression of Content-Type header. As people discovered in #86 and so, this header is not applied to GET request, which has its reason but axios also allows circumventing it by providing `data: null` or `data: {}` in request config.

A proper documentation on any part of this magical loop will help:
- Educate developers that Content-Type is only sensical on POST/PUT/PATCH where the request has a body.
- Clarify that `data` has its effect on GET method, as opposed to the quoted above.

#### Relevant File(s)

README.md at root

title: Relative URLs don't work as baseURL in 0.20 (browser)
body:
On 0.19, I used to set baseURL to a relative URL like this:
```
axios.defaults.baseURL = '/api'
```
This would append `/api` to the current `window.location.host`, like this:
```
axios.get("/contracts/1/invoices") // GET https://{window.location.host}/api/contracts/1/invoices
```
On 0.20, setting baseURL like this has no effect. 
This occurs in all major browsers.

title: Built-in Brotli Support (not decompress: false + transformResponse workaround)
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1635#issuecomment-603258750 suggest a way to support brotli however...

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I think this should be included in the library, as brotli has become very common nowadays and is supported by many browsers. If axios on client(browser) support Brotli content, server should support too.

Most cloudflare resources now served as brotli encoding.
And some node.js popular packages, for instance, [koa-compress](https://github.com/koajs/compress) for koa.js has support for brotli compression. [compression](https://github.com/expressjs/compression/pull/172) for express.js is on the way too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
Surely we can achieve this by `{ decompress: false }` + `transformResponse()` but we have to deal with the same logic and handle it like http adapter does internally (detect content-encoding headers and remove content-encoding headers). 

I think this should be supported by native.
Node.js < 10 has reached EOL so that means all stable node.js support brotli now.
And you can keep the backward compatibility by checking the function exists ( Like what PR #2071 did) .

#### Additional context
We have been using patched axios for a long time. Hope this can be a built-in feature in this great library.

#### Describe the bug
In situations that use Basic auth and do not pass the parameter "password" _**requestHeaders.Authorization**_ is concatenated unduly "**: undefined**".

#### To Reproduce
Any request using **Basic Authentication** without passing the parameter "**password**" as an example below.

```js
var axios = require("axios")
const instance = axios.create();
instance.request({
    method: 'POST',
    baseURL: ".../XPTO",
    auth: { username: "janedoe" }}
    ).then(
        // do something
    );
```

#### Expected behavior
To maintain compatibility with previous versions, the proper behavior would be to test if the parameter "**password**" was passed, otherwise concatenate empty.

#### Describe the issue
Wondering what the best approach is to use axios instances in a bunch of service objects. If I have an axios instance per service object and I end up with a lot of service objects, is this a bad design and/or going to bloat the app?

#### Example Code
```js
// /////////////////////////////////////////
// AXIOS API OBJECT
// /////////////////////////////////////////
import axios, {
  AxiosRequestConfig, AxiosInstance, AxiosError, AxiosResponse,
} from 'axios';

export default class ClientAPI {
  private api: AxiosInstance;

  public constructor(config?: AxiosRequestConfig) {
    this.api = axios.create(config);
    this.api.defaults.baseURL = 'http://localhost:8080';

    this.api.interceptors.response.use(
      (response: AxiosResponse) => this.responseIntercept(response),
      (error: AxiosError) => this.responseInterceptError(error),
    );

    this.api.interceptors.request.use(
      (params: AxiosRequestConfig) => params,
      (error: AxiosError) => console.log(error),
    );
  }

  public request(params: AxiosRequestConfig) {
    return this.api.request(params);
  }

  private responseIntercept(response: AxiosResponse) {
    console.log('ClientAPI Response intercepted: ', response);
    return response;
  }

  private responseInterceptError(error: AxiosError) {
    return console.log('ClientAPI Error Intercepted: ', error);
  }
}

// /////////////////////////////////////////
// BASE SERVICE OBJECT
// /////////////////////////////////////////
import { AxiosRequestConfig } from 'axios';

/**
 * Base class for a Service Object
 */
export default class BaseSvc {
  private _name: string;

  private _config: AxiosRequestConfig;

  public constructor(config: AxiosRequestConfig) {
    this._name = '';
    this._config = config;
  }

  name() {
    return this._name;
  }

  config() {
    return this._config;
  }
}
// /////////////////////////////////////////
// EXAMPLE SERVICE OBJECT
// /////////////////////////////////////////
import ClientAPI from '@src/config/clientApi';
import BaseSvc from './BaseSvc';

/**
 * Authentication service
 */
export default class AuthSvc extends BaseSvc {
  private api: ClientAPI;

  constructor(config: { url: string }) {
    super(config);

    this.api = new ClientAPI({ url: config.url });
  }

  name() {
    return 'AuthSvc';
  }

  public login() {
    return this.api.request({ url: 'api/v1/blah' });
  }
}

// /////////////////////////////////////////
// SERVICES 
// can pull this into vuex or anywhere
// else in the app
// /////////////////////////////////////////
import AuthSvc from './AuthSvc';

export const authSvc = new AuthSvc({
  url: '/auth',
});

// just an example of another service, could be like 5 or more diff services
const authSvc2 = new AuthSvc({
  url: '/auth2',
});

const Services = { authSvc, authSvc2 };

export default Services;

// /////////////////////////////////////////
// USAGE vue property instance
// /////////////////////////////////////////
import Vue from 'vue';

import router from '@router';
import store from '@state';

import App from './App.vue';
import AppServices from './services';

Vue.prototype.$services = AppServices;

new Vue({
  router,
  store,
  render: (h) => h(App),
}).$mount('#app');

// So, then the above can be used like so in vue components:
this.$services.authSvc.login()

// /////////////////////////////////////////
// USAGE vuex
// /////////////////////////////////////////
import axios from 'axios';
import {
  GetterTree, MutationTree, ActionTree,
} from 'vuex';

import { authSvc } from '@src/services';

//... state..

// ... mutations ...

// ... getters ...

export const actions: ActionTree<State, RootState> = {
   // Logs in the current user. just a super rough example of usage
  async logIn(context, { username, password }: { username: string; password: string }) {
    const { dispatch, commit, getters } = context;
    if (getters.loggedIn) return dispatch('validate');

    const response = await authSvc.login();
    const user = response.data;
    commit('SET_CURRENT_USER', user);
    return user;

  },
}



```

#### Expected behavior, if applicable
It seems that an axios instance per service object should be used but not sure if that is a bad practice or if their is a design flaw to that approach. There could be several service objects so if we create an axios instance per object is it going to bloat our app?

If one axios instance is used for all, then the api endpoint will have to be set on one axios instance for each service request which doesn't seem right.

#### Environment
- Axios Version 0.20.0
- Vue Version 2.6.12
- Node.js Version 12.18.3

#### Describe the bug
A clear and concise description of what the bug is. **If your problem is not a bug, please file under Support or Usage Question**


I am trying to use Axios to send an https request to a server with a self-signed certificate. however, the latest release version 0.20.0(https://github.com/axios/axios/releases/tag/v0.20.0) NEVER worked for me, however,  0.19.0 (https://github.com/axios/axios/releases/tag/v0.19.0) works.

I digged a bit on the source code and think the follow code changes could be the root caused:
```
commit 1b07fb9365d38a1a8ce7427130bf9db8101daf09
Author: Joshua Melvin <joshua.melvin@outlook.com>
Date:   Fri Sep 13 08:35:59 2019 -0400

    Fixing issue 2195 - order of if/else blocks is causing unit tests mocking XHR. (#2201)

diff --git a/lib/defaults.js b/lib/defaults.js
index 7cb8a25..23e1cbd 100644
--- a/lib/defaults.js
+++ b/lib/defaults.js
@@ -15,13 +15,12 @@ function setContentTypeIfUnset(headers, value) {

 function getDefaultAdapter() {
   var adapter;
-  // Only Node.JS has a process variable that is of [[Class]] process
-  if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && Object.prototype.toString.call(process) === '[object process]') {
-    // For node use HTTP adapter
-    adapter = require('./adapters/http');
-  } else if (typeof XMLHttpRequest !== 'undefined') {
+  if (typeof XMLHttpRequest !== 'undefined') {
     // For browsers use XHR adapter
     adapter = require('./adapters/xhr');
+  } else if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && Object.prototype.toString.call(process) === '[object process]') {
+    // For node use HTTP adapter
+    adapter = require('./adapters/http');
   }
   return adapter;
 }
```

title: Use `unknown` type instead of `any` for Typescript definitions of response types
body:
https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/basic-types.html#unknown

TL;DR `unknown` is the type safe equivalent of `any`. 

When getting `data` from `AxiosResponse`, the caller should be forced to make assertions about the response type. Using `any` can cause subtle programming errors. These errors won't be caught by most linter configurations, as they can only enforce the absence of the `any` type from first party code.

This would be a breaking change, so it might have to be saved for Axios v1.

title: If paramsSerializer is not specified, brackets are not encoded
body:
#### Describe the issue
The default behavior of paramsSerializer does not encode square brackets.
There cannot be brackets in place of the url parameter, and it should be encoded.

Looking at [this pull request](https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/49) or [this comment](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1111#issuecomment-334707256), This behavior seems to be intentional.

But according to the RFC 3986 cited there:
>  A host identified by an Internet Protocol literal address, version 6
[RFC3513] or later, is distinguished by enclosing the IP literal
within square brackets ("[" and "]").  This is the only place where
square bracket characters are allowed in the URI syntax.

(page 19)

URL parameter is not in this case. So I think brackets should be encoded in default behavior.

#### Example Code

```js
axios.get('/test', {params: {a: '[]'}})
```

#### Expected behavior, if applicable
expected : request URL is `https://domain.com/test?a=%5B%5D`
actual: request URL is `https://domain.com/test?a=[]`

body:

- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the bug
A breaking change was introduced here:
https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/2844/files?file-filters%5B%5D=.js&hide-deleted-files=true#diff-597f69416721110963cbbdf72c6d4e6e30d77da5073041b4b10a702c0a7186f0R76

Previously a `GET` request would be able to include `data`, since before the change above `util.merge` would keep the data property passed in `config`. Now the `mergeConfig` function will ignore the data property in `config`, causing the request to be made without data.

Whether or not a `GET` request should be able to send a body is debatable I guess, but this change should probably be documented somewhere.

#### To Reproduce
```js
var utils = require("./utils");
var mergeConfig = require("./core/mergeConfig");

console.log("--- mergeConfig --- ");
console.log(
  mergeConfig(
    { data: { hello: "world" } },
    {
      method: "get",
      url: "https://test.com",
    }
  )
);

console.log("--- utils.merge ---");
console.log(
  utils.merge(
    { data: { hello: "world" } },
    {
      method: "get",
      url: "https://test.com",
    }
  )
);
```

Result:
```
--- mergeConfig --- 
{ url: 'https://test.com', method: 'get' }
--- utils.merge ---
{ data: { hello: 'world' },
  method: 'get',
  url: 'https://test.com' }
```

#### Expected behavior
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

title: Post size limit in android with react-nativ
body:
#### Describe the issue
Hi.
I am using Axios in a react project that builds both for web and mobile app with react-native.
I am currently using version 0.20.0 that is currently the last.
Looking at the previous issues I was not able to find any prior solution.

Everything is good except when I try to do a multipart/form-data post with some files (server is under my control and available via https).
On some conditions, axios raises an empty exception before sending anything to the server, other times it goes good.

After some tests and search in the previous issues and other pages in internet (yes, stackoverflow too) I was able to identify the condition of the error: the size of the post request.

For requests below 1E6 bytes (I didn't traced down to the exact number, but 1MiB seems already over) I can send several files without any problems.
If I try to send even a single file, but greater than 1MB, axios gives the error without sending anything to the server.

Problem is always reproducible.

I get the file through document-picker in android. The uri in this case is content://something and it is passed via a FormData object.

#### Example Code

```js
const form = new FormData();
form.append("jsonData", someJsonString);
form.append("fieldName", fileObject);

const api_base = axios.create({
    baseURL: "https://someserver.com/api/",
});
const header = {
    "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data",
    "Authorization": "Token sometoken",
};
api_base.post("savemethod", form, { headers: headers})
    .then((res) => { /* if ok */ })
    .catch((err) => { /* if not ok */ });
```

#### Expected behavior, if applicable
It works under browser. Should work in android too

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.20.0

#### Describe the bug
In cases where `axios` is used by servers to perform http requests to user-supplied urls, a proxy is commonly used to protect internal networks from unauthorized access and [SSRF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Server-side_request_forgery). This bug enables an attacker to bypass the proxy by providing a url that responds with a redirect to a restricted host/ip.

#### To Reproduce
The following code spawns a proxy server that *always* responds with a 302 redirect, so requests should never reach the target url, however, `axios` is only reaching the proxy once, and bypassing the proxy after the redirect response. 

https://runkit.com/embed/1df5qy8lbgnc
```js
const axios = require('axios')
const http = require('http')

const PROXY_PORT = 8080

// A fake proxy server
http.createServer(function (req, res) { 
    res.writeHead(302, {location: 'http://example.com'})
    res.end()
  }).listen(PROXY_PORT)

axios({
  method: "get",
  url: "http://www.google.com/",
  proxy: {
    host: "localhost",
    port: PROXY_PORT,
  },
})
.then((r) => console.log(r.data))
.catch(console.error)
```

The response is the rendered html of _http://example.com_

#### Expected behavior
*All* the requests should pass via the proxy. In the provided scenario, there should be a redirect loop.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [0.21.0]
 - Node.js Version [v12.18.2]

Add any other context about the problem here. If applicable, add screenshots to help explain.

#### Describe the bug
HTTPS over HTTP Proxy Fails with 500 handshakefailed on mcafee proxy.
`mcafee initialize server context:handshakefailed:server state 1:state 9:Application response 500 handshakefailed`
With HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY set, curl works but axios.get fails.

#### To Reproduce

```ts
import axios from 'axios';

(async () => {
  try {
    console.log(await axios.get('https://github.com/'));
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(e);
  }
})();

```

#### Expected behavior
Request should succeed.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [0.21.0]
 - Node.js Version [v12.18.3]
 - OS: [OSX 10.15.7]

#### Current workaround
Install `global-agent`, remove the HTTP_PROXY env vars and set GLOBAL_AGENT_HTTP_PROXY.

Add `import 'global-agent/bootstrap';` to index.

title: axios serialization of "null" fields into "{}"
body:
#### Describe the issue

I have an object and I send it from client (JS) to the backend (in C#) using: POST

This is the sample: 

```js
const data = {
 item1: 10,
 item2: null
}
```
I expected on the backend to receive an object: ```{item1: 10,item2: null}```, but I receive ```{item1: 10,item2: {}}```

As you see the second item is converted from ***item2: null*** to ***item2: {}***. Well, this breaks my backend serialization, for nullable objects, as {} cannot be converted to nullable int. 

As mitigation for now, I added ```JSON.stringify(data)``` before POST-ing the objects, however this is a hack, and I would like to replace it with what should be here.

#### To Reproduce

***The config for content-type is:*** 
```Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8```

There is nothing special about this setting, I'd expect this to work with default settings. 

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [latest]
 - Adapter [XHR/HTTP]
 - Browser [Chrome]
 - Browser Version [86.0.4240.183]
 - Node.js Version [latest]

#### Describe the bug
Axios v.0.21.0 causes node.exe to silently crashing, without possibility to catch the exception.
Occurs with node.js v.14.15.0 (current LTS Version, recommended for most users).
Earlier or later versions works Ok (I have tested v.9.11.1 and v.15.1.0)

#### To Reproduce
Effect is not stable and not easy to be quickly reproduced, appears mostly on bad/slow internet connections. Most probably because of “connect ETIMEDOUT”, but this is only my guessing, because node.exe just unexpectedly terminates, without any additional info.

```js
// This is example code for reproducing the problem. Actually nothing special, just continuously getting lots of data. 
// Size of retrieved files is not important (from several kilobytes to several megabytes)
// MyApi is url/config of service-now.com REST API. Unfortunately I can’t share it.
var axios = require('axios');
let n=1;
test();
async function test() {
  do {
    await axios.get(MyApiUrl,MyApiConfig)
      .then(res => console.log(n++, "got "+JSON.stringify(res.data).length+" bytes (node.js "+process.version+")"))
      .catch(err => {console.error("ERROR: "+err.message);process.exit()})
  } while (true)
};
```

#### Expected behavior
Even on more or less normal internet connection node.exe crashes within getting of one or two gigabytes of data (in summary, by portions, not at once).
Choosing bad internet connection will bring the same result faster.

#### Describe the bug

I'm about download a static *.json file (used for localization messages), sending "Accept: application/json" and receiving "Content-Type: application/json".     promise = axios.get(`app/i18n/messages/${lang}.json`, {
```js
      headers: {Accept: "application/json"}

      // response.data can be string or object depending on parse failure
```

#### Expected behavior

body:
I have a weird inconsistancy regarding redirects and axios version 0.20.0 in a Mocha test in an async function.
First I log into an Express app which redirects to the main menu

login: finding user admin
POST /login 302 139.788 ms - 37
GET /settings/index 200 17.437 ms - 2218

    √ 1. Login as administrator (300ms)


Then we upload a large file. The request, as seen by Express looks like

{
  accept: 'application/json, text/plain, */*',  
  'content-type': 'multipart/form-data; boundary=--------------------------797269876434050357977005',  
  'access-control-allow-origin': '*',  
  cookie: 'sid=s%3AaQFv3KXS_Z8ycLbGfNJ7ESvXfyJUjylS.wyNUL91BFpBVhlbez97Tga4DoKMUgIJkU6tqYEYB9%2B4',  
  'user-agent': 'axios/0.20.0',  
  host: '127.0.0.1:22250',  
  connection: 'close',  
  'transfer-encoding': 'chunked'  
}

The upload extraction of data from the file takes some time and then when it finishes we get a timeout

Extractor finished
redirecting to /settings/library/index
POST /settings/library/upload 302 16858.270 ms - 45

    1) 2. Upload a tar file

  2 passing (1m)
  1 failing

 1) Test upload functions via express

       2. Upload a tar file:

     Error: Timeout of 60000ms exceeded. For async tests and hooks, ensure "done()" is called; if returning a Promise, ensure it resolves. (C:\Users\Jonathan\Project\test\unit\test-single.js)
      at listOnTimeout (internal/timers.js:549:17)
      at processTimers (internal/timers.js:492:7)

The Login, which processes the returned redirect uses this 

`
            reply = await Axios.post(serverUrl + loginPath,  
                        {username: 'admin', password: 'admin'},  
                        {jar: cookieJar,  
                         withCredentials:true,  
                         headers: {'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*'}  
                        });  
            expect(reply.status).to.equal(200);  
`

whilst the Upload uses this :-
`
            const formData = new FormData();
            formData.append('...','...');
            formData.append('uploadfile', stream);
            const formHeaders = formData.getHeaders()
            const request_config = {
                method: "post",
                url: serverUrl + uploadPath,
                jar: cookieJar,
                withCredentials:true,
                headers: {'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',...formData.getHeaders()},
                data: formData
            };
            reply = await Axios(request_config);
            expect(reply.status).to.equal(200);
`
The first POST with redirect is processed correctly, the second just times out. This is inconsistant.

If I add in an xhr header and react accordingly at the end of upload by returning a 200 response the test succeeds.
(Axios.defaults.headers.common['X-Requested-With'] = 'XMLHttpRequest')

Why?

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the bug
When using a response reject interceptor, the AxiosError object does not contain the original message in case of 503 Server Unavailable HTTP status code.

#### To Reproduce
Code snippet to reproduce, ideally that will work by pasting into something like https://npm.runkit.com/axios, a hosted solution, or a repository that illustrates the issue. **If your problem is not reproducible, please file under Support or Usage Question**

```ts
import axios, { AxiosRequestConfig, AxiosInstance, AxiosResponse, AxiosError, CancelToken } from 'axios';
import { StatusCodes } from 'http-status-codes';

var client = axios.create(config); // config only defines base URL and some auth headers
client.interceptors.response.use(undefined, (error: any) => {
        if (axios.isCancel(error)) {
          // Request cancelled
          return;
        }
        const axiosError = <AxiosError<any>>(error);
        if (axiosError && axiosError.response && axiosError.response.status === StatusCodes.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE) {
          const displayMessage = axiosError.response?.data ?? axiosError.response?.statusText ?? axiosError.message; // tried checking every place where the message could be
          console.log(displayMessage);
        }
      });

...

client.post(resourceUrl); // resource url points to the resource for the POST action
```

#### Expected behavior
I expected that I can access my custom error message somewhere in the AxiosError object, but I only see the 'Request failed with status 503' message in the debugger (this might happen for other 4xx statuses also). My custom status seems to be visible only under an internal field (**axiosError.request._response**).

#### Environment
 - Axios Version: 0.20.0
 - Adapter [e.g. XHR/HTTP]
 - Browser: react-native with Chrome debugger
 - Browser Version: Chrome version 86.0.4240.198 (Official Build) (64-bit)
 - Node.js Version: 13.7.0
 - OS: Android simulator on Windows 10
 - Additional Library Versions: React Native 0.63.3

#### Additional context/Screenshots
Here are some screenshots to with the response I get. Is there any way to make the **axiosError.request._response** available to the interceptor? It doesn't seem right to use the private property for the server custom message (which I added both in body and reason phrase as text in the server response).

This is what I can access from the request
![axios503error](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7274664/99958970-f1321b00-2d92-11eb-8c01-fafb1101b10f.PNG)

This is what I want to get - the custom message
![axios503error-internal-custom-message](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7274664/99958974-f2634800-2d92-11eb-8f0c-ee82dc25a82d.PNG)

title: Axios recognizes 401 wrong and lost all the config in a case of a heavy request
body:
#### Describe the bug
I use JWT to protect the backend. As soon as an access token is expired the backend sends 401 back, my front-end sends the request to regenerate a new token, and then resend the primary request.

But I found that if the request is heavy (for example, when you upload pictures, or have a lot of data inside) axios can't recognize the response properly. I see the network problem or some other stuff where the backend actually sent the normal 401 response:


So, basically the same code works properly or doesn't depending on the size of the sent data. I found 300> KB already causes this problem. It looks like an axios bug.

#### To Reproduce
Code snippet to reproduce, ideally that will work by pasting into something like https://npm.runkit.com/axios, a hosted solution, or a repository that illustrates the issue. **If your problem is not reproducible, please file under Support or Usage Question**

```js
// Just a normal post but data should be big:

let response = await axios.post('/app/api/entity/', obj); // Obj is a big object
```

#### Expected behavior
Axios should recognize the response when its status is 401.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.19.0
 - Browser Chrome 87.0.4280.66
 - OS:  Win 7
 - React 16.11.0

#### Additional context/Screenshots
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6174408/100166426-f61dca00-2e79-11eb-85c6-8279319c03d1.png)

You can see on the screenshot the part of VS Code showing it sends the 401 successfully and the browser console below showing the network error.
