#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
When a response contains a large number we lose some precision.  E.g:
```
{ "data": 1000000000000100000001 }
```
becomes
```
{ "data": 1.0000000000001e+21 }
```
which equals `1000000000000100000000`, not `1000000000000100000001`.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like to update the default response transformer to use the `json-bigint` parser.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
My current work around is to do this in my own code:
```
    const requestObjToSend = {
        ...
        transformResponse: [function transform(data) {
            // Replacing the default transformResponse in axios because this uses JSON.parse and causes problems
            // with precision of big numbers.
            // https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/6642ca9aa1efae47b1a9d3ce3adc98416318661c/lib/defaults.js#L57
            /* eslint no-param-reassign:0 */
            if (typeof data === 'string') {
                try {
                    data = JSONBig.parse(data);
                } catch (e) { /* Ignore */ }
            }
            return data;
        }],
    };

const response = await axios(requestObjToSend);
```

#### Additional context
No additional context

Feature Request: Support developers to customize return types in the interceptors.

I was using `interceptors` like
```js
axios.interceptors.response.use(function (
  response: AxiosResponse<YApiResponseBody>
): YApiResponseBody {
  return response.data
},
```
However, I got the error

> Argument of type '(response: AxiosResponse<YApiResponseBody>) => YApiResponseBody' is not assignable to parameter of type '(value: AxiosResponse<any>) => AxiosResponse<any> | Promise<AxiosResponse<any>>'.

Yeah, I know the error means, however, I just want to return the `response.data` directly. How can I accomplish that?

#### Describe the solution you'd like

I was thinking if `AxiosInterceptorManager` can accept `any` in `onFulfilled`

```diff
export interface AxiosInterceptorManager<V> {
- use(onFulfilled?: (value: V) =>V | Promise<V>, onRejected?: (error: any) => any): number;
+ use(onFulfilled?: (value: V) =>any , onRejected?: (error: any) => any): number;
  eject(id: number): void;
}
export interface AxiosInstance {
  (config: AxiosRequestConfig): AxiosPromise;
  (url: string, config?: AxiosRequestConfig): AxiosPromise;
  defaults: AxiosRequestConfig;
  interceptors: {
    request: AxiosInterceptorManager<AxiosRequestConfig>;
    response: AxiosInterceptorManager<AxiosResponse>;
  };
//...
}
```
I have seen https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1510 and https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/1605/files.

title: Axios returning data from another call
body:
#### Describe the bug
When I have multiple calls using axios to my backend, the calls will get muddled up with each other.

#### To Reproduce
I called a "/initialize" and a "/featured" endpoint to my backend using axios. Both happening simultaneously, with "/initialize" happening slightly earlier
 
```
axios({
    headers: {
        Authorization: 'xxxx'
    },
    method: 'get',
    url: 'http://localhost:8000/***/initialize'
}).then(response => {
    const axiosData = response.data
})
axios({
    headers: {
        Authorization: 'xxxx'
    },
    method: 'get',
    url: 'http://localhost:8000/***/featured'
}).then(response => {
    const axiosData = response.data
})
```

Upon inspection of response, I found the following:
![axios_error_marked](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48837852/101231901-30446280-36e9-11eb-896e-d0fdee6d5f4e.png)

The URL is that of "/featured" but it is returning data that is supposed to be returned from "/initialize". This problem will disappear if I limit the queue to 1 call each time. Then essentially the data that is supposed to be returned from '/featured' will be missing.

#### Expected behavior
"data" should return that from the "/featured" call, not from "/initialize". It seems like axios went to replace the call and mix up the data returned.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version: 0.19.2 (I have tested with axios 0.21 and problem still occurs)

title: Axios Proxy Issues - 501 and SSL errors
body:
#### Describe the bug
Getting weird error messages when passing a proxy into an Axios request. I've tried to add a `proxy` parameter to the following `GET` request and I get a `501` error code and when I then add a `protocol` parameter to the `proxy` object I get an `openssl` error

Note that I don't have any of these issues when using the library `axios-https-proxy-fix`, https://www.npmjs.com/package/axios-https-proxy-fix

#### To Reproduce
```javascript
axios
    .get(prod, {
        proxy: {
            host: proxy.host,
            port: proxy.port,
            auth: {
                username: proxy.userName,
                password: proxy.password,
            },
        }
    })
```

Then I tried adding `protocol` to the `proxy` object, like so:
```javascript
axios
    .get(prod, {
        proxy: {
            protocol: "https",
            host: proxy.host,
            port: proxy.port,
            auth: {
                username: proxy.userName,
                password: proxy.password,
            },
        }
    })
```

Error:
```bash
write EPROTO 17828:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:c:\ws\deps\openssl\openssl\ssl\record\ssl3_record.c:332:
```

I observe a memory leak when I pipe two requests with a file and I get the error "Request body larger than maxBodyLength limit"

#### To Reproduce

Bellow there a sample code:

```js
const optsGetFile = {
  method: "get",
  url: "http://localhost:7001/download",
  responseType: "stream",
};
const optsUploadFile = {
  method: "post",
  url: "http://localhost:7001/upload",
};

axios(optsGetFile)
  .then(({ headers, data }) => {
    return axios(_.assign(optsUploadFile, { data, headers }));
  })

```
The entire test code is present at [https://github.com/jose-lopes/test_axios](https://github.com/jose-lopes/test_axios) .

```
node test_fakeserver.js
```

```
mprof run node test.js
```

* execute 20 /record requests with interval of 30 seconds

```
for test in $(seq 1 20); do curl -X POST localhost:7000/record; sleep 30; done
```


The execution produces the next graph:

![Test Result](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jose-lopes/test_axios/master/images/test.png)

#### Expected behavior

I expected no memory leak even we got the error "Request body larger than maxBodyLength limit".
I executed again the test with option maxBodyLength: 30*1024*1024 and got the next graph without memory leak.

-->

#### Describe the bug
After upgrading our node version to v14.15.1 our Axios requests in our express server never receive a response from an endpoint that returns 204 with header: 'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked'.
I know we should not be receiving this ([see here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/912863/is-an-http-application-that-sends-a-content-length-or-transfer-encoding-with-a-2)) but we do not have control of this endpoint.

Previously when we were on v10.23.0 of node we had no problem with receiving these responses. 

I have tried the same request with the [request](https://www.npmjs.com/package/request) library and am able to receive a response. See example below. 

#### To Reproduce
Created a simple express server to demonstrate.

**npm install axios express request**

With the following **index.js**

Sending a GET request to http://localhost:8555/request will return 200 OK, whereas the request to http://localhost:8555/ will timeout/never receive a response.

```js
const express = require('express');
const axios = require('axios');
const request = require('request');

const httpPort = 8555;

const app = express();

app.get('/', async (req, res, next) => {
  try {
    const result = await axios.get(`http://localhost:${httpPort}/sample-upstream-response`, {
      timeout: 10000,
    });
    res.send(result.data);
  } catch (error) {
    res.sendStatus(500);
  }
});

app.get('/request', (req, res, next) => {
  request(`http://localhost:${httpPort}/sample-upstream-response`, { json: true }, (err, response, body) => {
    if (err) { 
      return res.sendStatus(500);
    }
    res.send(body);
  });
});

app.get('/sample-upstream-response', (req, res, next) => {
  res.writeHead(204, {
    'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked',
  });
  res.end();
});

app.listen(httpPort, () => {
  console.log(`INFO: listening on http://localhost:${httpPort}`);
});
```

#### Expected behavior
I am expecting that Axios should be able to receive the response from this server. Or I should be able to change some axios config to be able to receive this response.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [0.21.0]
 - Node.js Version [14.15.1]
 - Additional Library Versions [express 4.17.1, request 2.88.2]

#### Describe the bug
I am using axios on various node.js page monitors (over 40 sites) and I noticed that on a couple of them, the application suddenly crashes after calling await axios(options) or axios(options).then(). No error is thrown, nothing gets received into the .catch() code block. This issue only happens after the application runs for some time in a while(true) loop, but isn't related to memory usage. I guess there's some unhandled stuff that makes the request stop without rejecting or resolving the Promise.

#### To Reproduce

```js
const axios = require('axios')

function getRandom() {
    return parseInt(Math.random() * 10**10);
}

function sleep(ms) {
    return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
}

const options = {
    url: `https://www.walmart.com/cp/api/get-deals-list?prg=desktop&dealsId=christmas-deals&ps=60&page=1&shelf_id=7662948&shelfType=manual&${getRandom()}=${getRandom()}`, // this is an example endpoint with the same behaviour as the one I'm using, sorry but I can't share the exact one
    headers: {
        "accept": "application/json",
        "accept-language": "it-IT,it;q=0.9,en-US;q=0.8,en;q=0.7,fi;q=0.6",
        "content-type": "application/json",
        "user-agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_14_6) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/86.0.4240.198 Safari/537.36"
    },
    responseType: 'json'
};

(async () => {
    while (true) {
        let res
        try {
            res = await axios(options) // also tried with axios(options).then(res => {...})
        } catch(err) {
            if (err.response) {
                console.log(err.response.status)
            } else {
                console.log(err.toString())
            }
            continue
        }; console.log(res.status)
        await sleep(2500)
    }
})();
```

#### Expected behavior
Application keeps running and throws an error if any is caught, but instead it just stops after some hours of running

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [0.20.0]
 - Node.js Version [14.15.1]
 - OS: [Ubuntu 16.04 and Ubuntu 20.04]

title: Support AbortSignal for aborting requests
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Node 15 has built-in support for `AbortController` and `AbortSignal` and request cancellation propagates all the way up to [`http.request`](https://nodejs.org/api/http.html#http_http_request_url_options_callback) taking a signal parameter.

It would be useful to be able to abort an axios request using `AbortSignal`s:

```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const { signal } = ac;

axios({
  method: 'get',
  url: 'http://example.com',
  signal,
}).then(...);
ac.abort(); // aborts the above request with an `AbortError`
```

#### Describe the solution you'd like

Basically, axios already supports `CancelToken`s which are very similar to `AbortSignal`s.

Basically:

 - Rename `cancelToken` to `signal` (and support the old API for compatibility.
 - Allow passing an `AbortSignal` in. 
 - Listen to `abort` instead of doing `.promise.then` on the cancel token.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

Since AbortSignal is the primitive both the web and Node.js settled on - alternatives that I'd prefer would likely need to go through those bodies first probably.

#### Additional context

I'm happy to help with any issues or missing APIs from the Node.js side.

-->

#### Describe the bug
Different response types in node and in browser for the same responseType property 'arraybuffer' - in nodejs response.data is Buffer, but in browser it is ArrayBuffer. This behaviour is confusing and not documented.
#### To Reproduce

Nodejs:
```js
var axios = require('axios');
function isUndefined(val) {
            return typeof val === 'undefined';
}

function isBuffer(val) {
            return val !== null && !isUndefined(val) && val.constructor !== null && !isUndefined(val.constructor)
                && typeof val.constructor.isBuffer === 'function' && val.constructor.isBuffer(val);
}

function isArrayBuffer(val) {
            return toString.call(val) === '[object ArrayBuffer]';
}
var c = { responseType: 'arraybuffer' }
axios.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1', c).then(res => console.log(isArrayBuffer(res.data))).catch(ex => console.log(ex));
axios.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1', c).then(res => console.log(isBuffer(res.data))).catch(ex => console.log(ex));
```

Browser:
```js
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Buffer test</title>
</head>
<body>
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/axios/dist/axios.min.js"></script>
    <script>
        function isUndefined(val) {
            return typeof val === 'undefined';
        }

        function isBuffer(val) {
            return val !== null && !isUndefined(val) && val.constructor !== null && !isUndefined(val.constructor)
                && typeof val.constructor.isBuffer === 'function' && val.constructor.isBuffer(val);
        }

        function isArrayBuffer(val) {
            return toString.call(val) === '[object ArrayBuffer]';
        }
        var c = { responseType: 'arraybuffer' }
        axios.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1', c).then(res => console.log(isArrayBuffer(res.data))).catch(ex => console.log(ex));
        axios.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1', c).then(res => console.log(isBuffer(res.data))).catch(ex => console.log(ex));
    </script>
</body>
</html>
```

#### Expected behavior
Both response types should be ArrayBuffer

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.19.2
 - Node.js Version 14.12.0

#### Additional context/Screenshots
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest/Sending_and_Receiving_Binary_Data

```js
      'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
    },
    put: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
    },
    patch: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
    },
    other: 'stuff'
}
```

With axios v0.21.1

```js
axios.create({
    headers: {}
    baseURL: `${config.baseUrl}/api`,
    withCredentials: true,
    timeout: 3000,
  })
```

=> settled headers
```js
{
    other: 'stuff'
}
```

#### Expected behavior
Keep same default headers between two versions (or announce a breakchange)

#### Temporary fix

```js
import defaultAxiosConfig from 'axios/lib/defaults'

axios.create({
    ...defaultAxiosConfig,
    baseURL: `${config.baseUrl}/api`,
    withCredentials: true,
    timeout: 3000,
  })
```

Regards

#### Describe the bug
GET request gets CORS error using axios, but identical request works with xhr.

#### To Reproduce
Found the problem when I was investigating why google search stopped working in one of my projects. Yes the google api is configured correctly. This exact same query worked before axios version update. This worked on axios@0.19.2. I've seen similar problems in other axios webrequests, but this is a concrete example I had at hand.
```js
// gets CORS error
const res = await axios.get('https://www.googleapis.com/customsearch/v1/siterestrict?...');

// works without problems
const response = await new Promise(resolve => {
      const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();

      xhr.open('GET', `https://www.googleapis.com/customsearch/v1/siterestrict?...`);
      xhr.onload = function () {
        if (this.status >= 200 && this.status < 300) resolve(JSON.parse(this.responseText));
        else resolve({ err: '404' });
      };
      xhr.send();
    });
```

#### Expected behavior
Queries google custom search API without any problems.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.21.1
 - Browser Chrome, Brave, Firefox
 - Browser Version latest

#### Additional context/Screenshots
I've seen like 3 other Issues created about this, but those are blatantly ignored because of some arbitrary issue formatting rules.

title: mergeConfig.js may not be properly defaulting url anymore
body:
#### Describe the issue
Since `axios@0.20.0-0` the `url` config parameter has stopped merging the default instance value if one exists. This question is similar to #3491 that was auto-closed.

It looks like duplication of the `url` key was addressed in [this comment](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/2878#issuecomment-610269234), PR #2844, and 24b8ce3b1b636fb9a058d3710ee699a9157b7a3e

I am wondering if this change had an unintended side effect of not using the instance value if the passed in config does not contain a `url` key.

I believe that removing `url` from `valueFromConfig2Keys` and adding it to `defaultToConfig2Keys` in [mergeConfig.js](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/core/mergeConfig.js#L18-L26) would solve this and not reintroduce the duplication mentioned before, but I'm not sure if that would have other unintended consequences.

#### Example Code

```js
const instance = axios.create({ url: 'https://someexample.com' });

instance.request({ method: 'GET', params: { foo: 'bar' } }); // after merge occurs, this config will not have a url key
```

#### Expected behavior, if applicable
The `url` should default to the passed in value, if one exists. If not, then the default should come from the instance's config.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [^0.20.0-0]
 - Adapter [core]
 - Browser [N/A]
 - Browser Version [N/A]
 - Node.js Version [N/A]
 - OS: [N/A]
 - Additional Library Versions [N/A]

#### Additional context/Screenshots
Having to pass a `url` to `instance.request()` may be the desired behavior, but I wasn't sure where else to ask

Merging of `url` currently happens [here](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/core/mergeConfig.js#L48-L52)

When `url` is not present, none of the other merges can add a `url` value from another config.

Moving `url` key to `defaultToConfig2Keys` should grab the value from the passed in config (current behavior) and merge from the default config when not found (past behavior) [here](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/core/mergeConfig.js#L56-L62)

title: Better error message for URLs missing protocol
body:
<!-- Click "Preview" for a more readable version --

Please read and follow the instructions before submitting an issue:

- Read all our documentation, especially the [README](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/README.md). It may contain information that helps you solve your issue.
- Ensure your issue isn't already [reported](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue).
- If you aren't sure that the issue is caused by Axios or you just need help, please use [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/axios) or [our chat](https://gitter.im/mzabriskie/axios).
- If you're reporting a bug, ensure it isn't already fixed in the latest Axios version.
- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
My initial impression after reading https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/490 and https://github.com/axios/axios/commit/7c89704262913cebd98f7a27918b92c87c48c9e1 is that Axios can handle URLs without protocol (ie. `www.google.com`) by defaulting to `http`. But when I try
```js
axios({
  method: "get",
  url: "www.google.com",
})
  .then(function (response) {
    console.log(response);
  })
  .catch(function (e) {
    console.log(e);
  });
```
an error was thrown:
```
Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:80
    at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (net.js:1146:16)
    at TCPConnectWrap.callbackTrampoline (internal/async_hooks.js:129:14) {
  errno: -61,
  code: 'ECONNREFUSED',
  syscall: 'connect',
  address: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 80,
  config: {
    url: 'www.google.com',
    method: 'get',
    headers: {
      Accept: 'application/json, text/plain, */*',
      'User-Agent': 'axios/0.21.1'
    },
    transformRequest: [ [Function: transformRequest] ],
    transformResponse: [ [Function: transformResponse] ],
    timeout: 0,
    adapter: [Function: httpAdapter],
    xsrfCookieName: 'XSRF-TOKEN',
    xsrfHeaderName: 'X-XSRF-TOKEN',
    maxContentLength: -1,
    maxBodyLength: -1,
    validateStatus: [Function: validateStatus],
    data: undefined
  },
...
```

To figure it out, I looked into the [http adaptor](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/adapters/http.js#L91) and realized that https://github.com/axios/axios/commit/7c89704262913cebd98f7a27918b92c87c48c9e1 was adding a default protocol **for proxy only but not for the normal case**. 

So I thought about creating a PR to fix that but then I realized we are parsing the url using nodejs `url` module, but [`url` can't handle URL without protocol](https://github.com/nodejs/node-v0.x-archive/issues/8220), calling `url.parse('www.google.com')` generates:
```
Url {
  protocol: null,
  slashes: null,
  auth: null,
  host: null,
  port: null,
  hostname: null,
  hash: null,
  search: null,
  query: null,
  pathname: 'www.google.com',
  path: 'www.google.com',
  href: 'www.google.com'
}
``` 
whose pathname and path are totally wrong. And if the `url` module can't parsing the url correct, I think there is little Axios can do to provide support. The best option here is to explicitly state that Axios doesn't support urls without protocols and throw an error with that message.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
Explicitly state in the doc that Axios doesn't support incomplete URLs (ie. `www.google.com`) and throw an error when receiving such URL through `url` or `baseURL`.

body:
#### Describe the bug
This bugreport very similar to #315 which was implemented and fixed, however I think this is not solved yet. When the query params parsing process itself fails (before the request even started), the resulting error object does not contain request information, making it hard to debug, especially with as error reports.

#### To Reproduce
```js
axios.get("", {
  params: {
    someParam: new Date(undefined)
  }
}).catch((e) => {
  console.log(e);
})
```

```
RangeError: Invalid time value
    at Date.toISOString (<anonymous>)
    at parseValue (buildURL.js:53)
    at Object.forEach (utils.js:219)
    at serialize (buildURL.js:51)
    at Object.forEach (utils.js:225)
    at buildURL (buildURL.js:38)
    at dispatchXhrRequest (xhr.js:45)
    at new Promise (<anonymous>)
    at xhrAdapter (xhr.js:13)
    at dispatchRequest (dispatchRequest.js:53)
```

#### Expected behavior
I would expect the error to have information about the request (uri, config, etc) just like when the error is thrown on server response error.

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I'm using http adapter when I test modules with `nock` which is  mocking api library and want to send a request which has data which is form-data.
```js
    const data = new FormData()
    data.append('test', files[0])
    await axios.post('http://localhost:3333', data)
```
And I found out an error occurs `'Data after transformation must be a string, an ArrayBuffer, a Buffer, or a Stream'`.
It's because nodejs's http doesn't support form-data as data [see](https://nodejs.org/api/http.html#http_request_end_data_encoding_callback)

#### Describe the solution you'd like
Why don't we add error message for data which type is form-data?
ex)
```js
    if (data && !utils.isStream(data)) {
      if (Buffer.isBuffer(data)) {
        // Nothing to do...
      } else if (utils.isArrayBuffer(data)) {
        data = Buffer.from(new Uint8Array(data));
      } else if (utils.isString(data)) {
        data = Buffer.from(data, 'utf-8');
     // For example:
     } else if (utils.isFormData(data) {
        return reject(createError('FormData is not allowed as data in http.', config)
      } else {
        return reject(createError(
          'Data after transformation must be a string, an ArrayBuffer, a Buffer, or a Stream',
          config
        ));
      }
```

#### Additional context
I implemented an example [see](https://github.com/qkreltms/axios-with-http-adapter).

#### Describe the bug
Uploading of multiple files produces empty array but referring one of the files or different single file is working fine.

#### To Reproduce
1) Using FormData object to append files.
2) Using axios API with data as FormData object.
3) This works fine when a single image is uploaded or one of the files alone is passed to axios data (ex- .files[1]). 

```js
This is my index.js:

const form = document.querySelector('.form')
if(form) {
    form.addEventListener('submit', e => {
        e.preventDefault()

        const formData = new FormData()
        formData.append('images', document.getElementById('file-upload').files)    // Line - 7 (console logged the element and it contains all the image files selected.) 
        
        addFiles(form)
    })
}


This is the module of axios API call:

import axios from 'axios'
export const addFiles = async data => {
    try {
        const res = await axios({
            method: 'POST',
            url: 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/resources',
            data
        })

        if(res.data.status === 'success') {
            console.log('Files added')
        }  
    } catch(err) {
        console.log(err)
    }
}
```

#### Expected behavior
Note: I am using **multer** package for processing the images.

When using **Postman** for the request, there is no issue with multiple files(images), the issue arises when I use axios to hit my api.
When I upload multiple files and request via axios, the **req.files** have - [] in the multer's middleware. 
But when I send like **.files[0] instead of .files** in Line - 7 (index.js), the req.files have the specified indexed image.

Uploading of a single file as no issues, as the **req.file** contains the image.

#### Describe the issue
I have some issues understanding how Axios handles Content-Type (when automatically detected and manually set) and what Axios does to body content regarding the content-type, if any. Note: Some of my questions may be a naivety of js (not my daily driver). I have seen some talk about this, but not in a completely conclusive way. Thank you for any provided information.

#### Example Code
First off, I am setting the Content-Type to `application/json` explicitly, as the request body content needs to be a valid json literal string. In this example, I am not passing an object, just a simple value.
```js
var data =  "test";
axios
  .post("some-endpoint", data, {
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
  })
  .then((res) => {
    HandleRequestSuccess(res);
  })
  .catch((err) => {
    HandleRequestError(err);
  });
```
The resulting request payload is `test` with no wrapped quotes, so it is not a valid Json literal. 

I would have expected that the quotes would be in there... however this may be a misunderstanding of some js basics to begin with.

Even if I take out the var and wrap the quotes directly in the post call, the same result persists.

body:
#### Describe the issue

I use  Axios to get request from my golang webserver. (json)

But i find the response was not correctly transformed into json.

#### Example Code
Code snippet to illustrate your question

```js
export function listFinancialrecord(query, options) {
  return request({
    url: '/financialrecords',
    method: 'get',
    params: {
      query: query,
      options: options
    },
    paramsSerializer: function (params) {
      const query = Qs.stringify(params.query)
      const options = Qs.stringify(params.options)

      let querystring = query

      if (querystring) {
        if (options) {
          querystring = querystring + '&' + options
        }
      } else {
        if (options) {
          querystring = options
        }
      }
      return querystring
    },
  });
}
```

author: sebnapi

title: Axios 0.21.1 and 0.20.0 not merging url with baseURL
body:
#### Describe the bug
I was just encountering the problem locally, that the new axios version is not merging `url` with `baseURL`. I found some issues with version 0.19.0 Issue #2190 where the params are not merged. I used the runnable example to showcase my problem:


#### To Reproduce
https://runkit.com/sebnapi/axios-0-21-1

```js
const axios_newer = require("axios@0.21.1");

const ctr_args = {
    baseURL: "https://httpbin.org",
    url: "/anything",
    params: {
      q: "question",
    }
  };

axios_newer.request().then(function(r) { console.log("axios 0.21", r.data); }).catch(function (e) {console.log(e)})
```

#### Expected behavior
Request gets fullfilled with uri appended to baseURL.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.21.0, 0.20.0, 0.19.0

#### Additional context/Screenshots

![Screenshot 2021-03-03 at 14 48 50](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/539707/109823196-9e88ba80-7c2f-11eb-8bf9-7007e87910de.png)

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
My problem is that I get type errors if I try to add custom properties to the AxiosRequestConfig parameter. I have a project built in TypeScript where I'm using interceptors to log information about requests being made. For certain request I'd like to include parts of the payload in the log itself.

For example, let's say I have a function
```
function updateProduct(product: Product) {
  return axios.put(`/products/${product.id}/`, product)
}
```
This function may be called multiple times, in multiple places in my app. Every time a product is updated, I want to include the product name and quantity in the request log. The request log is being made in my interceptor:
```
axios.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
  console.log('API Request', {
    url: config.url,
  })
  return config
})
```


The issue I'm facing is with the type AxiosRequestConfig. If I simply ignore the type, I can pass the data that I want to log through this parameter, like this.
```
function updateProduct(product: Product) {
  return axios.put(`/products/${product.id}/`, product, {
    metadata: {
      product_name: product.name,
      product_quantity: product.quantity,
    }
  })
}

axios.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
  console.log('API Request', {
    url: config.url,
    metadata: config.metadata,
  })
  return config
})
```

#### Describe the solution you'd like
Make AxiosRequestConfig type extensible.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
Ignoring the type. // @ts-ignore

#### Describe the bug I am working with a (not really clean/modern) PHP backend I don't have any control over. When there is a server error, it sometimes responds with bare php error printouts or simple html code, not formatted in JSON. In these cases, we don't get something like a "invalid format" exception from axios we could handle, but instead a cryptic JS error saying `e.sent.data.forEach is not a function`. title: I assume axios handles 304, but I don't see a 304 in the source code?
body:
In plain vanilla JavaScript or jQuery, it would use

https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/main/src/ajax.js
```js
isSuccess = status >= 200 && status < 300 || status === 304;
```
because `304` is "not changed".  I wonder how come axios doesn't have to deal with `304`... or perhaps browsers have built in mechanism to change `304` to a `200`? Or else a `304` comes back and axios wants a status code between 200 and 299 and treats it as not ok?  Could there be a line in docs or comment to clarify it too?

title: Cannot completely remove User-Agent header
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Some APIs only work if the User-Agent header is entirely omitted.  This is not currently possible in Axios in NodeJS.  #1411 opened this discussion some time back, but was closed without an actual solution other than commenting out the code which inserts the header.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
There should be a way to completely omit the U-A header if desired.  User-Agent is not a required header, and its deprecation (in favor of Client-Hints) is being actively discussed.

The simplest solution would probably to retain the current behavior if no User-Agent header is specified, but omit the header if it is explicitly provided with a falsy value (`null` and `""` both seem to clearly communicate the caller's intent not to have a value here).

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
Explicit options to disable the current behavior could work, but that seems like a less-elegant path.

title: Add the possibility to specify which implementation of XMLHttpRequest to use
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Right now it's not easily possible to use Axios in a Firefox add-on, if one wants to make a request they're supposed to use "content.XMLHttpRequest" not "XMLHttpRequest". [Reference here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/Content_scripts).
The work around would be to implement a whole new adapter which would be a great deal of work considering the very high number of config options handled in there.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

Extend AxiosRequestConfig to add
`export interface AxiosRequestConfig {
...
getXMLHttpRequestImpl?: () => XMLHttpRequest;
...
}`

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
An alternative would be to work on the adapter feature, to have as little as possible code in it, so that creating a new adapter wouldn't mean having to handle dozen of features.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Yes. 
When fetching and sending data as form data, the user is required to manually build a form data object. 
- If the data is nested, building form data isn't trivial, and can result in an inappropriate structure and bugs. 
- If the data already exists as an object or array, the user needs to write his own solution to convert an object to form data.  

#### Describe the solution you'd like
Provide a reliable easy way to convert object to form data. 

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
I couldn't find a simple existing solution to easily convert a nested object to form data. 

#### Additional context
Since form data is only used (as far as I know) in the context of fetching, I thought Axios should provide this functionality. Perhaps export a function that can convert an object to form data, or add a property to AxiosConfig and handle the conversion internally. 

If relevant I'd be happy to submit a PR.

body: #### Describe the issue Following suggestions on issue #647, I'm using the CancelToken feature to implement a timeout instead of the `timeout` parameter. I'm getting a similar behavior to #904 even though I'm creating a **new** cancel token for every request, all requests made after the timeout limit are cancelled (see screenshot). I am using the `axios-rate-limit` to create a custom instance of axios instead of using the default, not sure if that causes an issue. I have both GET and POST requests but the result is the same. If this is the intended behavior, how do I actually make a request obey its own unique CancelToken? #### Example Code ```js const ax = require("axios"); const axios = rateLimit(ax.create(), { maxRequests: 5, perMilliseconds: 1000}); const timeout = 1000; //ms async foobar(){ return axios.get(endpoint, { cancelToken: new ax.CancelToken(function executor(cancel) { setTimeout(() => {cancel(`Timeout of ${timeout} ms.`)}, timeout); }) }) .then((res) => {...} .catch((error) => {...} } // also tried async foobar(){ const abort = ax.CancelToken.source() const id = setTimeout( () => abort.cancel(`Timeout of ${timeout}ms.`), timeout ) return axios .get(url, { cancelToken: abort.token, ...options }) .then(res => { clearTimeout(id) ... }) .catch((error) => {...} } ``` #### Expected behavior, if applicable I some saw suggestions ([here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61081268/axios-cancel-token-cancelling-every-request) and [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44852054/cant-cancel-axios-post-request-via-canceltoken)) to cancel the previous canceltoken but my purpose is to fetch and update different records using the same endpoint but with unique ID, so I don't want to cancel the previous call. title: Date serialization in headers should use GMT
body:
#### Describe the bug
When the `If-Modified-Since` header is set to a `Date` object, Axios serializes it into a format containing the local timezone (GMT+2 in my case). [According to MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/If-Modified-Since#directives), HTTP dates should always be in GMT, and indeed, the web servers I tried ignore the header in the current format. Providing a valid string representation (eg. by using `Date.toUTCString()`) as the header value is a workaround.

#### To Reproduce
```js
const axios = require("axios")
const date = new Date()
//const date = new Date().toUTCString()

axios.get("https://i.imgur.com/JOKsNeT.jpg", {headers: {"If-Modified-Since": date}})
    .then(resp => console.log(resp.status))
    .catch(e => console.log(e.response.status))
```
https://runkit.com/embed/hxh6dsdcyqrr

#### Expected behavior
The above code should print 304, because the image is older than the specified date. 

#### Environment
 - Axios Version: 0.21.1
 - Adapter: HTTP
 - Node.js Version: 12.17.0
 - OS: Windows 10

#### Describe the bug
On node js axios is not able to tell that the URL has been redirected.

#### To Reproduce
```js
async function getData(url) {
  const response = await axios('https://sofifa.com/players?col=oa&sort=desc&set=true&offset=10980&r=70001');
  if (response.request._redirectable._redirectCount) throw 'Redirected';
  const html = response.data;
}
```

#### Expected behavior
Axios should have returned with 1 as redirectcount but its returning 0.
#### Environment
 - Axios Version [^0.21.1]
 - Node.js Version [e.g. 14.15.0]
 - OS: [OSX 11.2.3]

title: Increased response time after too much cancelled request
body:
I use live search. And i cancel previous request when new key pressed by user. But response time is too much when there is a lot of cancelled requests before last one. Ex: User pressed 10 times to keys. 9 request has been cancelled. The last one takes 3 seconds to response. If pressed 20 times to keys. 19 request has been cancelled. The last one takes 6 seconds to response. Less cancelled tokens before last request means faster response.

I use Laravel for api. Is there any solutions for this issue?

title: maxBodyLength does not work with disabled redirects
body:
#### Describe the bug

maxBodyLength does not work with disabled redirects like when using `{ maxRedirects: 0, maxBodyLength: 100 }` in options.

#### To Reproduce

```js
require("axios")
	.put("http://www.example.com", Buffer.alloc(1000), { maxRedirects: 0, maxBodyLength: 100 })
	.catch(e => console.log("axios returned error:", e));
```

#### Expected behavior

It should print something like:
```
axios returned error: Error [ERR_FR_MAX_BODY_LENGTH_EXCEEDED]: Request body larger than maxBodyLength limit
...
```

As this example does:
```js
require("axios")
	.put("http://www.example.com", Buffer.alloc(1000), { maxBodyLength: 100 })
	.catch(e => console.log("axios returned error:", e));
```

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.21.1
 - Adapter HTTP
 - Node.js Version v15.12.0

#### Additional context/Screenshots

title: each axios request is recognized as a new user.
body:
My vue js project is running at 3000 port and my express project is running at 4000 port.

I'm logging in with Axios, creating a session. But a second request is perceived as a new session.

There is no such thing in "postman". It only happens in the browser. Actually, I don't know exactly where the problem is, but I need to figure it out. Can you help me?

So that does not happen in "postman"? Then the problem is how can I solve this in axios.

title: Passing timeout as a string is throwing an error in the latest version of axios due to upgrade of follow-redirects
body: #### Describe the bug Axios uses `follow-redirects` internally for making http requests. When axios was using follow-redirects@1.13.3, we were able to supply timeout in string, e.g. '30000'. Recently, `follow-redirects` upgraded to v1.14.0. Upon supplying the timeout as a string, eg. '30000', follow-redirects@1.14.0 is throwing the following error: ` ERROR Uncaught Exception { "errorType": "TypeError", "errorMessage": "The \"msecs\" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('30000')", "code": "ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE", "stack": [ "TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The \"msecs\" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('30000')", " at validateNumber (internal/validators.js:125:11)", " at getTimerDuration (internal/timers.js:381:3)", " at TLSSocket.setStreamTimeout [as setTimeout] (internal/stream_base_commons.js:250:11)", " at RedirectableRequest.destroyOnTimeout (/opt/nodejs/node_modules/follow-redirects/index.js:159:12)", " at RedirectableRequest.emit (events.js:314:20)", " at RedirectableRequest.EventEmitter.emit (domain.js:483:12)", " at ClientRequest.eventHandlers. (/opt/nodejs/node_modules/follow-redirects/index.js:14:24)", " at ClientRequest.emit (events.js:326:22)", " at ClientRequest.EventEmitter.emit (domain.js:483:12)", " at tickOnSocket (_http_client.js:709:7)" ] } ` #### To Reproduce ```js var axios = require("axios") response = axios({ url: 'https://www.google.com', method: 'GET', timeout: '30000' }).then(res => { console.log('res:', res) }).catch(err => { console.log('err:', err) }) ``` Try the above code with follow-redirects version v1.13.3 and v1.14.0. You will find that the error is thrown when you are using v1.14.0 and the code runs fine when using v1.13.3. #### Expected behavior No error thrown by the code. #### Environment - Axios Version: 0.21.1 - Node.js Version: 12.x, 14.x - OS: [e.g. iOS 12.1.0, OSX 10.13.4] - Internal dependency: follow-redirects@1.14.0 #### Additional context/Screenshots

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the bug
Not working properly when using inside vm.runInNewContext. It does not recognise the config params as plain objects so it replaces the default configs with param config instead of merging them.

The current isPlainObject implementation: 
```js
function isPlainObject(val) {
  if (toString.call(val) !== '[object Object]') {
    return false;
  }

  var prototype = Object.getPrototypeOf(val);
  return prototype === null || prototype === Object.prototype;
}
```
fails to recognise the received object as plain because the Object.prototype is not the same reference in both contexts:
```bash
✗ node
Welcome to Node.js v12.19.0.
> const vm = require('vm');
> const prototype = Object.prototype
> console.log('out: ' + (prototype === Object.prototype));
out: true
> vm.runInNewContext('console.log("in: " + (Object.prototype === prototype))', { prototype, console });
in: false
```

#### To Reproduce
This works as expected when running on node:
```js
var axios = require("axios");
const instance = axios.create({
  baseURL: "https://google.com",
  headers: { "default-header": "value" }
});
instance.interceptors.request.use(function (config) {
  console.log("request headers: " + JSON.stringify(config.headers));
  return config;
});
instance.get("/", { headers: { "new-header": "value2" }});
```
```
> request headers: {"common":{"Accept":"application/json, text/plain, */*"},"delete":{},"get":{},"head":{},"post":{"Content-Type":"application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},"put":{"Content-Type":"application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},"patch":{"Content-Type":"application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},"default-header":"value","new-header":"value2"}
```

Same code run inside new context does not:
```js
const vm = require('vm');
const content = ' \
const axios = require("axios"); \
const instance = axios.create({ \
  baseURL: "https://google.com", \
  headers: { "default-header": "value" } \
}); \
instance.interceptors.request.use(function (config) { \
  console.log("request headers: " + JSON.stringify(config.headers)); \
  return config; \
}); \
instance.get("/", { headers: { "new-header": "value2" }}); \
';
vm.runInNewContext(content, {
  require,
  console
});
```
```
> request headers: {"new-header":"value2"}
``` 

#### Expected behavior
Same behavior running with ```vm.runInNewContext``` than running in main context

#### Environment
 - Axios: 0.21.1
 - Node.js: v12.19.1
 - OS: OSX 10.14.6

#### Additional context/Screenshots
Add any other context about the problem here. If applicable, add screenshots to help explain.

The axios timeout is response timeout, not connection timeout. Firstly, this is not properly documented. Also, a request connection timeout is really handy and can avert many errors and bugs.

title: Support setting the `highWaterMark` in Node.js
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/39092

The way a `Readable` in Node.js works, it will require a full iteration of the event loop every time it receives more than `highWaterMark` amount of data. For a network stream going at 20MB/s this amount to at least 320 iterations per second or no more than 3ms of processing time per chunk.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

Setting `highWaterMark` to a higher than the default 16k value when constructing the `Readable` allows for processing of high bandwidth streams with ease.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

The only other solution is to not do (almost) anything else when downloading at high speeds.

#### Additional context
The Node.js issue discusses the problem in detail
https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/39092

```javascript
axios.interceptors.request.use(async (config) => {
  const accessToken = await authService.getAccessToken();

  if (!accessToken) {
    return invalidToken(); // this is firing sometimes
  }
  return {
    ...config,
    headers: {
      ...config.headers,
      authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`
    }
  };
}, (error) =>
  Promise.reject(error)
);
```

As I commented above, `invalidToken()` fires somewhat randomly. Sometimes a user authenticates, returns to our app, our APIs return data, then the app triggers a reauth because it goes to `invalidToken` because the `accessToken` is empty.

```javascript
axios.interceptors.request.use(function (config) {
  config.headers.test = 'I am only a header!';
  return config;
}, null, { synchronous: true });
```

#### Describe the issue
I currently have an issue on one project in which we have 2 tabs and pressing each tabs makes a different API call and these calls populate a graph. The issue here is that if I press one tab and quickly press another before the request is over, I'll have the wrong graph on the tab that I just pressed.
I was looking for a way to solve this and saw `axios.cancel()` and decided to give it a go, but, after doing the setup, what I'm seeing is that all the calls made after calling `axios.cancel()` are getting cancelled and that's not the intended behaviour for my app.

#### Example Code
Here's my API call

```js
export const getDifferentialData = (
  sourceId: string,
  sourceLine: string,
  source: any
) => {
  const graph1Request = getData(
    sourceId,
    sourceLine,
    source
  )
  const graph2Request = getData(
    sourceId,
    sourceLine,
    source
  )

  return Promise.all([graph1Request, graph2Request]).then(results => {
    const [graphA, graphB] = results

    return {
      graphA: parsedData(graphA),
      graphB: parsedData(graphB),
    }
  })
}

export const getData = (
  sourceId: string,
  sourceLine: string,
  source?: any
) => {
  if (sourceId && sourceLine) {
    return api.get(`apiGoesHere`, { cancelToken: source.token }).then(response => {
        const { data } = response
        return parsedData(data)
      })
  } else {
    return api.get(`apiGoesHere`, { cancelToken: source.token }).then(response => {
        const { data } = response
        return parsedData(data)
      })
  }
}
```

My `Graph` has a `Tabs` component inside with an `onChange` prop that triggers `userDidChangeTab`. That `userDidChangeTab` triggers `fetchGraph`

```js
const Graph: FC<Props> = () => {
  const source = axios.CancelToken.source();

  // we ensure that the query filters are up to date with the tab selected
  const userDidChangeTab = (tabIndex: number) => {
    const isDifferentialTabSelected = isDifferentialTab(tabIndex)
    let newFilters = queryFilters

    if (isDifferentialTabSelected) {
      newFilters = {
        // props go here
      }
    } else {
      newFilters = {
        // props go here
      }
    }

    source.cancel()

    fetchGraph(isDifferentialTabSelected)
    setActiveTab(tabIndex)
  }

  // Function to fetch two differential graphs.
  const fetchGraph = (isDifferential: boolean) => {
    setFetching(true)

    if (isDifferential) {
      getDifferentialData(
        sourceId,
        sourceLine,
        source
      )
        .then(({ graphA, graphB }: any) => {
          setGraphData(graphA)
          setMatchData(new diffMatch(graphA, graphB, 1.0))
        })
        .catch(reason => {
          const errorMessage = errorMessageFromReason(reason)
          addMessageToContainer(errorMessage, true)
        })
        .finally(() => {
          setFetching(false)
        })
    } else {
      getGraph(
        sourceId,
        sourceLine,
        source
      )
        .then((graphData: any) => {
          setGraphData(graphData)
          setMatchData(null)
        })
        .catch(reason => {
          const errorMessage = errorMessageFromReason(reason)
          addMessageToContainer(errorMessage, true)
        })
        .finally(() => {
          setFetching(false)
```

#### Describe the bug
Response interceptors are supposed to be triggered when there is problem with the response as [documented](https://github.com/axios/axios#interceptors). But an offline network condition - which caused a failed request - somehow triggered the response interceptor, resulting in `err.response` to have `undefined` value.


#### To Reproduce
1. Register the interceptor as shown below
2. Simulate offline network condition in Chrome DevTools
3. Make a request with axios

```js
axios.interceptors.response.use(null, (thrown) => {
  console.log({ ...thrown }); // thrown.response is `undefined`
  
  switch (thrown.response.status) { // ⚠️ throwing Error!
    // ...
  }
});
```

#### Expected behavior
`thrown.response` should be guaranteed to exist in a response interceptor.

#### Environment

#### Describe the bug
Some servers are not sending a zlib header in their deflated data. CURL had the same problem and implemented a "fix" for it: https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/5c932f8fe9dad94a7417702958ffa9e8db67c549/lib/content_encoding.c#L227-L229

Axios is also returning a `Z_DATA_ERROR` in this case.

#### To Reproduce

Use axios to request a page without a zlib header in the deflated data (e.g. https://www.konicaminolta.eu/eu-en/about-us/corporate-book) and force it to only accept deflate encoding.

```js
let url = 'https://www.konicaminolta.eu/eu-en/about-us/corporate-book';
let config = {
  headers: { 'Accept-Encoding': 'deflate' }
};

await axios.get(url, config);
```

#### Expected behavior

Getting the correctly inflated data.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [0.21.1]

```js
    headers: {

    params: {
      X: 'Y',

  API.interceptors.request.use((request) => {

    return request;
  });

  API.interceptors.response.use(
    (response) => {
      console.log('Response:', stringify(response, 4));
      return response;
    },
    (err) => {
      console.log('Response error:', stringify(err, 4));
```

The result is a string that contains the xml.

title: Why use axios if there is a fetch.
body:
I want to understand the advantages of using axios compared to fetch. I suggest that everyone write an example code that will show why you are using axios or an example code that you think will be difficult to repeat using fetch. And I will throw off a simple example code that will do the same thing but using fetch and the usual approaches of writing code.

I want to show with these examples that using fetch you can do everything the same as using axios, but for this you do not have to learn a new library, you just need to have basic programming skills. Or during the discussion, I will understand that axios is more optimal than fetch.

The problems you face when using axis, unlike fetch 1. You need to study a third-party library that was invented by ordinary developers, and fetch is used immediately in the browser. 2. This library may die sooner or later 3. Newcomers to the web will most likely know about the native fetch than axios 4. Axios has a very different interface than fetch, so knowing the native fetch library, you can't use axios and vice versa. 5 Since axios has various pre-configs, it can cause confusion that you do not need to pass a header if you pass json and so on, the library will think of a lot for you, and if there are questions, then you have to look at how it is implemented.

title: Axios with multiple accept header values
body:
#### Describe the issue
This is just a question about the behaviour of Axios. Should it work with multiple accept content types?

I have an API that can return multiple types, text/csv except when an error occurs, at which point json is returned. 

When a CSV file is returned and the content type is `text\csv` the file is automatically decoded by the browser as csv, but if I give axios multiple mime types then it no longer decoded.

If I remove the accept header completely then Axios sends three: `application/json`, `text/plain` and `*/*`, why does it add all three by default, why not just add `*/*`?

Is this the expected behaviour?

#### Example Code
Any request that sets two mime types using accept headers, e.g

`Accept: text/csvl, application/json`

#### Expected behavior, if applicable
For axios to respect whatever the server sets as the response content type instead of always choosing the first mime type it is passed.

For a csv file to be decoded when the response content type is csv, and the accept headers contain csv. This works if the only type supplied to axios is csv, if I supply two types then the CSV is no longer decoded.

This might not be specific to axios but I cannot really understand why this works as expected with only a single mime type or why axios by default (no header supplied) then sends three mime types as headers.

title: Export mergeConfig
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

We have a web frontend that supports multi-tenancy by contacting different backends depending on the data that was loaded by the 'main' backend. We manage several instances of `AxiosRequestConfig` to handle all the configuration parameters for the different backend services (usually default config per service which is then merged with per request config). We currently create an instance per request with the default config and then pass our request-specific config to `get`, `post`, and so on. We tried to use a singleton `AxiosInstance` per backend service, but this resulted in HTTP requests being performed one after the other instead of in parallel, which is not what we wanted.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

Our solution would be easier maintainable and testable if we could manage and merge the `AxiosRequestConfig` by ourselves. We would need access to the `mergeConfig` method, which unfortunately is not exported by default. 

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

We can do a deep import now, but need to create a separate TS module for that to work in our TypeScript-based projects. Alternatives are using an Axios instance per request as described in the first section.

#### Additional context

None.

- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I strongly sympathize with issue #3313, which was closed by BOT, and feel that it is an issue worth considering, so I will raise another issue with the same content.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I think that the type argument of the response should be changed from `<T = any>`  to `<T = unknown>`.

```ts
// <T = any>
const asyncFunction = async () => {
  const response = await axios.get('/path/to/endpoint')
  const data = response.data // any 😢
  const foo = data.foo // not type error, but foo may be undefined
  // ...
}
```

```ts
// if <T = unknown>
const asyncFunction = async () => {
  const response = await axios.get('/path/to/endpoint')
  const data = response.data // unknown
  // const foo= data.foo // type error
  if (hasFoo(data)) { // type testing is compulsory 😄 
    const foo = data.foo
    // ...
  }
}
```

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
This may be breaking changes, so it might be a good idea to just document the following wrappers.

```ts
async function typeSafeGet<T = unknown>(
  url: string,
  config?: AxiosRequestConfig,
) {
  return axios.get<T>(url, config)
}
```

#### Additional context
In https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/3002, @carloschida agrees that `unknown` is optimal choice.

body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
When using Axios we get type support for various properties, but headers is typed as 
```ts
Record<string, any>
```
Which means there is practically no type support. So if I want to send form data I need to accurately type
```js
'Content-Type': 'multipart/form-data'
```
This is time consuming, and can easily break.

title: Is it possible to improve type support for Headers
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
When using Axios we get type support for various properties, but headers is typed as 
```ts
Record<string, any>
```
Which means there is practically no type support. So if I want to send form data I need to accurately type
```js
'Content-Type': 'multipart/form-data'
```
This is time consuming, and can easily break. 

#### Describe the solution you'd like
AFAIK possible properties for HTTP headers is well defined. Then for a specific property such as  `Content-Type` the possible values are well known. 
Suggestion is to build a better type to represent Headers, and use it to type the headers parameter. 

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
I can't think of a relevant alternative.

#### Describe the bug
AxiosRequestConfig.params that contains a list is parsed incorrectly when calling axios.get(...) function

#### To Reproduce
For this method call
```ts
axios.get(' http://my.url.com/api/lotes'
   params {
      loteId: [1024,1480,1666,2021]
   }
}).then(response => console.log(response.data))
```

The answer is
> http://my.url.com/api/lotes?loteId[]=1024&loteId[]=1480&loteId[]=1666&loteId[]=2021

#### Expected behavior
It should be
> http://my.url.com/api/lotes?loteId=1024&loteId=1480&loteId=1666&loteId=2021

It's obviously a bug, since it's not respecting the https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6570 rules (see 1.2 and 3.2) and then no server implementation is going to accept it as correct.

It's been 5 years we are using crutchs¹ to workaround it . . . :disappointed: 

#### Environment

 - Browser [Firefox]
 - Browser Version [90.0]
 - Node.js Version [14.7.0]
 - Additional Library Versions [React 16.13.1]

¹ Brazillian idiomatic; means we are using a support that should be temporary, but is not

-->

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
A problem:
Currently axios contains interceptors, which are executed before standard handlers.
What we want to do: we want to have standard error handler, which will execute only if there is no local handler

#### Describe the solution you'd like
```javascript
import Toast from 'toast';

const axiosInstance = axios.create();

axiosInstance.defaultReject((error) => {
  if (['401', '403', '404'].includes(error.status.code)) {
    Toast(error);
  }
  // in case we don't expect that issue at all we fail-fast
  return Promise.reject();
})

// guess also makes sense for some cases
axiosInstance.defaultResolve();

axiosinstance.get('whatever').catch((error) => {
  if (error.status.code === 404) {
    // show user that something was not found
  }
  // axiosInstance.defaultReject will execute
  return Promise.reject(error);
})

// in case of error axiosInstance.defaultReject will execute
axiosinstance.get('whatever-another');

axiosinstance.get('whatever-another-smoething).catch((error) => {
  // only that handler will execute, and not axiosInstance.defaultReject
});
```

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
Currently only 1 alternative was found - copypaste "standardhandler" everywhere in catch

title: Host name spoofing
body:
<!-- Click "Preview" for a more readable version --

Please read and follow the instructions before submitting an issue:

- Read all our documentation, especially the [README](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/README.md). It may contain information that helps you solve your issue.

- If you're reporting a bug, ensure it isn't already fixed in the latest Axios version.
- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the bug
Axios uses old `url.parse` API which is vulnerable to [host name spoofing](https://hackerone.com/reports/678487). [Node issue](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/31279)


#### To Reproduce

```js
import axios from 'axios';
const url = `http://evil.com%2F.example.com/get`;
await axios({ url });
```


#### Expected behavior
Axios throws error on invalid URL.

As per `new URL` API this URL is invalid:
```
> new URL(`http://evil.com%2F.example.com/get`)
Uncaught TypeError [ERR_INVALID_URL]: Invalid URL
    at __node_internal_captureLargerStackTrace (node:internal/errors:464:5)
    at new NodeError (node:internal/errors:371:5)
    at onParseError (node:internal/url:552:9)
    at new URL (node:internal/url:628:5) {
  input: 'http://evil.com%2F.example.com/get',
  code: 'ERR_INVALID_URL'
}
```

But axios [uses](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/lib/adapters/http.js#L98) old API, which leads to request being made to `http://evil.com/%2F.example.com/get` (notice the slash before `%2F`). So that the real host is `evil.com`.

This may lead to security implications if URL is dynamically constructed like this:
```js
// id is user-controlled input
const url = `http://${encodeURIComonent(id)}.${host}/${someSecretInfo}/getSomething`
```
This case leads to SSRF

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.21.3
 - Adapter HTTP
 - Node.js Version 16.8.0


#### Additional context/Screenshots
None

#### Describe the bug

Version 0.21.1 and before did not. This gave extra 2KB fat for the minified build.

#### To Reproduce

```
$ curl -s https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/axios/0.21.4/axios.min.js | wc -c
   19157
$ curl -s https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/axios/0.21.2/axios.min.js | wc -c
   19025

$ curl -s https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/axios/0.21.4/axios.min.js | grep -c '"name":"axios","version":"0.21'
1
$ curl -s https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/axios/0.21.2/axios.min.js | grep -c '"name":"axios","version":"0.21'
1
$ curl -s https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/axios/0.21.1/axios.min.js | grep -c '"name":"axios","version":"0.21'
0
```

#### Expected behavior

Please keep `dist/axios.min.js` weight healthy. 💪

#### Environment

 - Axios Version 0.21.2 to 0.21.4

#### Additional context/Screenshots

This happens because [lib/helpers/validator.js](https://github.com/axios/axios/commit/5ad6994da#diff-a49cff66d6cc35c2eed6284efa2fd160f18c710edfbf0d7d48046b9cf5624f83R3) loads `package.json` even for `dist/axios.min.js` build. @DigitalBrainJS

#### Describe the bug

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the issue
I'm using axios in the browser.

Cancel token exceptions do not appear to correspond 100% with what Chrome developer tools considers a response failure.

Essentially I want to retry certain requests (even POST requests) if the server doesn't respond within `5000ms`. Obviously with non-idempotent requests it's important that success/failure of response matches the server.

So I tried to implement a connection timeout using the following code. A more simple version of this code is [here](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1739#issuecomment-581846543), and it has the same problem.

I noticed that **if I set the connection timeout to be as close as possible to the time it takes for server to respond (to emulate a request finishing right at the time out), there appears to be a race condition where cancel is retried even though it was successful**

I have tried `axios-retry` and it has the same issue.

#### Example Code
Code snippet to illustrate your question

```js
const makeRequest = async (args, connTimeout, responseTimeout) => {
  const source = axios.CancelToken.source();

  const argsWithToken = {
    ...args,
    cancelToken: source.token,
  };

  const api = buildAxios(responseTimeout);

  const timeout = setTimeout(source.cancel, connTimeout);

  return api(argsWithToken).then(result => {
    clearTimeout(timeout);
    return result;
  });
};

const handleRetries = (args, maxRetries) => (
  new Promise(async (resolve, reject) => { /* eslint-disable-line */
    let retries = 0;
    let success = false;

    while (!success && retries < maxRetries) {
      try {
        const result = await makeRequest(args, 300, 30000); /* eslint-disable-line */
        success = true;
        resolve(result);
      } catch (err) {
        retries += 1;
        // console.log(`Error making ${args.method} request to ${args.url}, retrying... #${retries}`);
      }
    }
    // line below is included to prevent process leaks
    if (!success) reject(new Error(`Retried ${retries} times and still failed: ${args.url}`));
  })
);

handleRetries({url: '/settings', method: 'get'}, 3)
```

#### Expected behavior, if applicable
I don't know if it's my code, a limitation of JS, or axios, but I would expect that cancel would never get called, as the timeout is cleared in the success callback.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [e.g. 0.18.0]: `^0.21.1`
 - Adapter [e.g. XHR/HTTP]: `XHR`
 - Browser [e.g. Chrome, Safari]: `Chrome`
 - Browser Version [e.g. 22]: `latest`
 - Node.js Version [e.g. 13.0.1]: `N/A`
 - OS: [e.g. iOS 12.1.0, OSX 10.13.4]: `OSX latest`
 - Additional Library Versions [e.g. React 16.7, React Native 0.58.0]: `vue 3`

- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the bug
A clear and concise description of what the bug is. **If your problem is not a bug, please file under Support or Usage Question**
When using binary data (ie. `Uint8Array`) with a buffer that has the `byteOffset`  and `byteLength` properties, those properties are ignored by `Axios`  and the entire buffer is sent through the wire. 

#### To Reproduce
Code snippet to reproduce, ideally that will work by pasting into something like https://npm.runkit.com/axios, a hosted solution, or a repository that illustrates the issue. **If your problem is not reproducible, please file under Support or Usage Question**

Here is a playground that reproduce this bug https://codesandbox.io/s/axios-playground-forked-40179?file=/src/index.js

To see the problem, check the Network panel of the dev tools and see that the request to `/` has 3 bytes (there should be only a single one)

```js
import axios from "axios";

const array = new Uint8Array([0, 1, 2]); // This creates a full Uint8Array 
const sub = array.subarray(0, 1); // We just use a slice of that array, then the underlying `ArrayBuffer` still has the entire array in memory but has now the `byteLength`  and `byteOffset` properties set. 

axios
  .post("/", sub, { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream" } }) // This will send 3 bytes to the server, it should send only one
  .catch(() => {}); 
```

#### Expected behavior
In the previous example a single byte should be sent in the payload of the request (instead of 3). 
The `byteOffset` and `byteLength`  should be read and interpreted by Axios.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.21.4
 - Browser Firefox
 - Browser Version 92
 - OS:  Ubuntu 20

Add any other context about the problem here. If applicable, add screenshots to help explain.

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
By default, an Axios instance is configured to follow redirects (`301`, `302`, `307` and `308`) automatically. However, you might want to exclude certain URLs from being opened, e.g. if they might contain malicious content or so. 

#### Describe the solution you'd like
It would be nice to be able to specify one or more URL patterns or host names which to exclude in redirects. For instance, if a redirect would point to `https://someevilwebsite.tld`, it would be convenient to tell Axios not to go there, but abort the request instead. 

Go's `http.Client` comes with a [`CheckRedirect`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/d0dd26a88c019d54f22463daae81e785f5867565/src/net/http/client.go#L64) handler, which fulfills exactly the purpose I described above. It might serve as an inspiration.

#### Describe the bug
This is similar to closed issue #315 . 
When trying to get the `response.request.data`, wrong data is returned. Instead of returning the **requests body**, the **responses body** is actually returned.
This makes it hard to use interceptors for cache-ing requests, where the requests body is significant. The `requests`  and `response.request` do not match, so cache keys would not match.

#### To Reproduce
If we configure request and response interceptors and log the request data in both, we can see that the response interceptor does not hold the same request as the request itself.   
An example is runnable on [RunKit](https://npm.runkit.com/axios)

```js
var axios = require("axios")
const instance = axios.create();

instance.interceptors.request.use((req)=>{
    console.log("req:",req.data);  // this is the requests data / body
    return req;
},
(err)=>{
    
});

instance.interceptors.response.use((res)=>{
    // this data should represent the the same thing, but it does not
    console.log("res:", res.request.data); 
    return res;
},
(err)=>{
  
});

// get a random URL and send some test data
instance.get("https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/networking/sockets/examples/EchoServer.java",{
    data:{
        "data":"test"
    }
}).then((r)=>{
   // do stuff
});
```

#### Expected behavior
Both `console.logs()` should yield exactly same result. in other words, `response.request === request`  should be the same 

#### Environment
 - Axios Version: 0.21.1
 - Adapter: HTTP
 - Browser: /
 - Browser Version: /
 - Node.js Version: v14.17.3
 - OS: Windows / Linux / hosted (runkit)

Everything needed is shown in the code example

Both of these projects will "run" on different subdomains, e.g. `api.domain.tld` and `app.domain.tld`. I am using axios within the Vue project to het anti xsrf tokens via cookies, after which axios automatically includes the xsrf token in the specified header for subsequent requests.

This all works fine in a local test environment where both the api and the app operate on the same domain (`localhost`) as also [stated on the Laravel documentation](https://laravel.com/docs/8.x/csrf). But this breaks when moving to a production or staging environment where the front-end and back-end operate on different subdomains.

 - Latest axios via npm 0.21.4

### Flow
1. Axios (JavaScript executing in a browser environment "from" **app**.domain.tld) requests a xsrf token from `api.domain.tld/sanctum/csrf-cookie` via a HEAD request.
2. Laravel Sanctum returns a response with a `set-cookie` header containing a new xsrf token.
2. Axios requests an xsrf protected action (such as a user registration request) from `api.domain.tld/api/register` via a POST request. **This request should now contain the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header, but it does not. It only does under a localhost testing environment.**

title: Maybe a bug in isURLSameOrigin function?
body:
#### Describe the bug

There is probably a bug in https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/7d6bddba2d8de29c263feaef4c40daa50cb4b176/lib/helpers/isURLSameOrigin.js#L56

If you pass `undefined`, the `parsed` variable becomes `undefined` and then you try to access `parsed.protocol`. Of course I wouldn't pass `undefined` intentionally, but if I have some config object and property is missing, then you get this unexpected behavior in browser.

#### To Reproduce

```js
const someConfigObject = {};
const opts = { url: someConfigObject.accidentallyNotExistingProperty };
axios(opts).then(response => console.log(response)).catch(e => console.log(e));
```

#### Describe the bug
When a request with a `timeout` is cancelled, the setTimeout for the timeout is not cleared, and prevents Node.js from exiting. In an app that cancels requests when closed, the app will successfully cancel requests but then hang until the timeouts expire.

#### To Reproduce
The code below will log a cancel error and then hang for 30 seconds before exiting.

```js
const cancelTokenSource = axios.CancelToken.source();

axios.get("http://google.com", { timeout: 30000, cancelToken: cancelTokenSource.token })
	.then(response => console.log(response.status))
	.catch(err => console.log(err));

setTimeout(() => cancelTokenSource.cancel(), 1);
```

#### Expected behavior
It should log a cancel error and immediately exit.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version 0.21.4
 - Node.js 14.16.0
 - Windows 10

#### Describe the bug
json in response body is not parsed as before.
In my Axios config I have `{ responseType: 'json' }` set.
Then classic way to get the json body would be something like 
```
someAxiosInstance.post('/some/api/endpoint')
  .then(function (response) {
    const { data } = response;
    // do something with data...
  }).catch(...)
```
This was all good and smooth. I recently updated axios in my previously working project, and errors start to be thrown, traced all the way to axios, where the `data` from response is simply just raw json object without being parsed. This is not true before my project last seen working fine with axios v0.21.1.
Manually parse json in `transformResponse` sure can work, but I think this is not axios intension to have user parse json manually?
Reversing back to v0.21.1 fixes everything. All versions since 0.21.2 seems to suffer the same issue. 

Read release logs, this does not seem to be an intended change, so I'd guess there might be a bug somewhere.
Tried v0.22.0 just released, many new typing related issues are showing up, e.g., `instance.defaults.headers` is now possible `undefined` and things like `instance.defaults.headers.common['Authorization']` becomes hard even if I put non-null assertion on `headers`, it still complains about `'Authorization'` is not a number and can not be used to index `common`. And `axios.isAxiosError()` as a type guard, now asserts response as `AxiosResponse<never> | undefined`, where the `never` generic parameter makes no sense, because it's common to retrieve api response from an error response, `never` intends to prevent this....


#### To Reproduce
Kinda tight in schedule now, can't prepare any sandbox to reproduce this, but they are all very basic setup and usage, would be very easy to reproduce in regular usage.

#### Expected behavior
If specified `responseType`  as 'json', response.data should be parsed to JS object instead of left as raw json string.

#### Describe the bug
When specifying an expected `response.data` type to the post method it also sets that expected type to the request body. Also, when not specifying a type, the type for the `response.data` gets inferred to be the same as the type of the request body. This leads to typescript errors in VS Code and during compile time when the response and request bodies in code doesn't have the same type (which is usually the case). This was not an issue in v0.21.4 - which I reverted to in order to get around this issue.

#### To Reproduce
 1. Install axios v0.22.0
 2. Add a type for the `response.data` like in this example:
```tsx
axios.post<ExpectedResponseBody>(`post url`, { foo: "bar" }, {});
```
Also look at the CodeSandbox example [here](https://codesandbox.io/s/axios-v0-22-0-type-issue-joty3?file=/src/App.tsx:897-1031)

#### Expected behavior
When specifying the expected type of the `response.data` in the post call, the request body shouldn't have the same expected type. And the inferred type for the request body shouldn't automatically get applied to `response.data`.
