title: Progress event does not have lengthComputable property
body:
### Describe the bug

I use axios to send requests in the browser. I recently updated from axios v0.22.0, and I'm noticing that `onUploadProgress` works a little differently from how it did before — enough that I had to change my code. Previously, the `onUploadProgress` callback was passed a native `ProgressEvent`. It's now passed an `axiosProgressEvent`. I like `axiosProgressEvent` and all the new properties available on it. However, there's one property that the `ProgressEvent` had that the `axiosProgressEvent` doesn't: `lengthComputable`. Previously, my code was using `lengthComputable`, so I had to change it. That wasn't hard to do, but I didn't realize I had to for a while, as I didn't see this change mentioned in the release notes. Going forward, I'll probably just use the `progress` property on the `axiosProgressEvent`, but it would have been nice not to change existing code.

`lengthComputable` is still accessible via the `event` property on the `axiosProgressEvent`, but I think it should also be a top-level property on the `axiosProgressEvent`. That would make `axiosProgressEvent` more like a superset of a native `ProgressEvent`.

### To Reproduce

_No response_

### Code snippet

```js
onUploadProgress: (event) => {
  // event no longer has a lengthComputable property.
  console.log(event);
}
```


### Expected behavior

I was expecting the `lengthComputable` property to continue to exist on the event passed to `onUploadProgress`. If it's possible, I think it'd be helpful to add `lengthComputable` to the `axiosProgressEvent`. Alternatively, this change could be highlighted in the release notes. I think this change was introduced in bdf493cf8b84eb3e3440e72d5725ba0f138e0451 as part of v1.0.0.

title: Security: Axios sends HTTPS data in cleartext to a proxy (regression)
body:
### Describe the bug

Axios use the HTTP proxy incorrectly, so that the data and URL is sent in plaintext to the proxy. The proxy then wrongly tries a TLS connection with the target server and fails.

Older axios versions work correctly. Other libs also work.

### To Reproduce

1. Set proxy environment variables, using `export http_proxy="http://foo:3100"` and export https_proxy="http://foo:3100" (the http:// is correct, because the HTTP client connects to the proxy via HTTP and does HTTPS on top)
2. `let r = await axios.get("https://www.beonex.com"); console.log("page", r.text());`



### Code snippet

```js
// with proxy, see above
let r = await axios.get("https://www.beonex.com");
console.log("page", r.text());
```


### Expected behavior

* The client connects to the remove server directly via TLS. The squid proxy only forwards the TCP stream, and is *not* involved in the TLS connection
* The proxy should not even see the URL (!), only the hostname.
* You see the HTML source of the webpage


### Actual behavior

* Error HTTP 503
* You see the HTML source of the squid proxy error page
* TLS connection settings mismatch between squid proxy (!) and remote server
* Page, with HTML and some text removed for readability:
"
The following error was encountered while trying to retrieve the URL: https://www.beonex.com/

Failed to establish a secure connection to [unknown]

TLS code: SQUID_TLS_ERR_CONNECT+GNUTLS_E_KEY_USAGE_VIOLATION
SSL handshake error (SQUID_TLS_ERR_CONNECT)

This proxy and the remote host failed to negotiate a mutually acceptable security settings for handling your request. It is possible that the remote host does not support secure connections, or the proxy is not satisfied with the host security credentials.
"
* You can see that the target URL is in the proxy error page. That's a serious security bug. (The proxy should never see the full URL in the first place. Ditto headers, cookies etc.)


### Axios Version

1.5.1

### Adapter Version

_No response_

### Browser

_No response_

### Browser Version

_No response_

### Node.js Version

18.15.0 (but not relevant, see below)

### OS

Ubuntu

### Additional Library Versions

_No response_

### Additional context/Screenshots

### Cause

The squid proxy should not even be involved in the TLS connection. By the very definition of it, HTTPS needs to connect straight from the browser to the target server, and no intermediate proxies should be involved in the TLS connection. Otherwise, that would defeat the entire purpose of the TLS connection, to prevent man in the middle to see the content. That's what the `CONNECT` is for in HTTP proxies: It simply tunnels the TCP connection, and the browser does TLS.

It appears that axios is driving the HTTPS proxy wrong and doesn't do a `CONNECT`, but lets the proxy connect to the target server via TLS. That would be wrong.

### What works

* Axios 0.27 works, axios 1.5.1 fails, so it's clearly a regression sometime in this version range. This also proves that it's a bug in axios. I haven't been able to narrow down the first faulty version yet that broke it.
* [ky](https://github.com/sindresorhus/ky) (version 1.2.3) works fine, again showing that it's likely a bug in axios.

_No response_

_No response_

### Additional context/Screenshots

The problem come from the commit [111811eadc849c08a3a2074930c50f68afa6eba5](https://github.com/axios/axios/commit/111811eadc849c08a3a2074930c50f68afa6eba5).

In **axios.js**, this check was added :
```js
if (paramsSerializer !== undefined) {
  validator.assertOptions(paramsSerializer, {
    encode: validators.function,
    serialize: validators.function
  }, true);
}
```
And `validator.assertOptions` throw the error when the first parameter isn't a object.

Moreover, the next line manage the case where `paramsSerializer` is a function :
```js
utils.isFunction(paramsSerializer) && (config.paramsSerializer = {serialize: paramsSerializer});
```

A solution will be to down the check after the below line transform `paramsSerializer` from function to object, so the check will be ok.

title: postForm's form-data serialization breaks for Blob in Node.js
body:
### Describe the bug

When I try to have `postForm` automatically serialize a `Blob` in Node.js, it fails with the error message `"Blob is not supported. Use a Buffer instead."` I dug into it a bit, and it seems the culprit is a combination of things.

### To Reproduce

1. Install the latest version of Node.js (at the time of writing: v21.7.3) and 
2. Run a server that accepts file uploads at `POST /api/upload` (or whatever endpoint you'd like)
3. Have an image file in the path `/tmp/image.jpg` (or wherever you'd like)
4. Run the code below in Node.js

### Code snippet

```js
const filename = "/tmp/image.jpg"

axios.postForm(
	"/api/upload",
	{
		"files": {file: await fs.openAsBlob(filename), filename}
	}
)
```


### Expected behavior

`postForm` serializes the object containing the `Blob` as `FormData` and uploads it successfully

### Axios Version

1.6.8

### Adapter Version

_No response_

### Browser

Node.js

### Browser Version

v21.7.3

### Node.js Version

v21.7.3

### OS

macOS 14.4.1

### Additional Library Versions

```bash
N/A
```


### Additional context/Screenshots

On [lib/helpers/toFormData.js:92](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/helpers/toFormData.js#L92), `formData` gets instantiated as `PlatformFormData`, which comes from the [`form-data`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/form-data) package. This probably shouldn't happen, since Node.js has its own built-in `FormData`. I'd suggest swapping the order of that `||` statement to have any environment's built-in `FormData` take precedence.

There's a long-standing bug in `form-data`, https://github.com/form-data/form-data/issues/396, wherein `FormData[Symbol.toStringTag]` is `undefined`. `FormData[Symbol.iterator]` is also `undefined`, but that's not covered in the issue. However, it is relevant here. The function `isSpecCompliantForm` ([lib/utils.js:632](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/utils.js#L632)) uses these to check whether whatever's getting passed in (`thing`) is indeed an instance of `FormData`. I'd suggest doing that a different way, such as using `instanceof`.

What does all this have to do with `Blob`? Well, for some reason that's beyond me, in `toFormData`, `isSpecCompliantForm` is tied to `useBlob` ([lib/helpers/toFormData.js:110](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/helpers/toFormData.js#L110)), the boolean that determines whether or not `Blob` is supported. In fact `Blob` is supported, by virtue of the fact that `_Blob` is defined in the previous line. I'd suggest decoupling these expressions, since bundling together `FormData` validation and `Blob` validation is too complex for one boolean, especially when the name of that boolean only references one of them. It unnecessarily breaks `Blob` support based on a bug in a third-party implementation of `FormData`—which, as you'll recall from earlier, we probably shouldn't even prefer to use in the first place.

Another question that comes to mind is: why do we even need to validate `FormData` at all here? Since we're already preferring a specific version of a third-party implementation of `FormData`, I think we can safely assume that what we have on our hands is actually a spec-compliant `FormData` (except, of course, for the finer details of `Symbol.toStringTag` where `form-data` differs from `FormData`). The only reason I can think of to validate `FormData` is if (as we should) we preferred to use the environment's built-in `FormData`, which might differ between environments. And doing that would actually fix this bug altogether.

title: XSRF-TOKEN logic should utilize cookie domain instead of current page domain
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When using `axios` to make HTTP calls to a backend server from a ui hosted at a different subdomain, the XSRF-TOKEN logic is not available and requires manually parsing out the cookie and passing the X-XSRF-TOKEN header yourself. This is because the logic that currently exists checks to see if the full domain of the page you're currently on matches the full domain of the api you're making a call to. 

https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/ab3f0f9a94853c821cb00f1112788ecdd3ae7ed1/lib/adapters/xhr.js#L191
https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/ab3f0f9a94853c821cb00f1112788ecdd3ae7ed1/lib/helpers/isURLSameOrigin.js#L55-L59

### Describe the solution you'd like

Instead of matching against the current page and the target api url, this logic could match the target api url against the XSRF-TOKEN cookie domain. Since the XSRF-TOKEN cookie will be sent along with the request to this domain regardless, there should no problem in also pulling out the cookie value and passing it as the X-XSRF-TOKEN header. 

### Describe alternatives you've considered

The alternative having the developer utilizing axios ensure that each axios call to the backend domain passes the withXSRFToken config as true, or building this logic into a withXSRFToken function config that does the cookie/target domain match itself.

### Additional context/Screenshots

Having static files for a Single-page Application (React) hosted via a CDN at a different domain than the backend is a relatively common practice which would benefit from this change.

title: PATCH requests using fetch adapter
body:
### Describe the bug

When using the fetch adapter, patch requests are failing

### To Reproduce

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/axios-patch-fetch-adapter-nmxp8t


### Expected behavior

Patch requests should succeed with fetch adapter

### Axios Version

v1.7.0-beta.1

### Adapter Version

fetch

### Additional context/Screenshots

This is because per spec (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#methods) methods are case-sensitive, and only some methods are normalized, but patch is not one of them.

The solution is to call `method.toUpparcase()` on 2 places:
https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/adapters/fetch.js#L125
https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/adapters/fetch.js#L149


Http and xhr adapters do this, probably because of the same reason mentioned above:
https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/adapters/http.js#L164
https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/adapters/xhr.js#L33

title: `null` parameters are getting passed in urls breaking requests in v0.x
body:
This PR to backport custom params serializer from v1 into v0: https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/6263

does not include the v1 fix outlined below (spotted by @FlorisVeldhuizen) around `null` params being pushed into the URL.

It looks like the changes to `toFormData.js` were not included in the backport: https://github.com/axios/axios/commit/b0ebf9fcacbab3e5a020a1a4d5d3837342d7dcd7#diff-8423b44acd3fb9f35b00404bfeed15aaf4659cdf06b879849c5026b4a05d2efa 

axios v0.28.1 will send blank params:

```
{
  foo: null,
  bar: 1
}

?foo&bar=1
```

axios v0.27 does not send blank params

```
{
  foo: null,
  bar: 1
}

?bar=1
```

>> It seems that `null` and `undefined` parameters are now getting passed as well in urls, breaking many requests. You can see this check being removed in #4734, I wonder how this breaking change that is not mentioned anywhere went under the radar

> Good catch; I wonder if we can update the main meat of their toString function for serializing the params to omit undefined and null. Feel free to make suggestions on #5108! I just wanted some of the old functionality back 😅

_Originally posted by @ChronosMasterOfAllTime in https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/5107#issuecomment-1276295059_

title: adapter fetch should pass fetchOptions to fetch function
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When I use `fetch` as `adapter` in Nodejs, there is (maybe) no way to use `ProxyAgent` as dispatcher provided by [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici?tab=readme-ov-file#undicifetchinput-init-promise) (which is the default implication of fetch API since [node v18 released](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/announcements/v18-release-announce#fetch-experimental)).

I expect the code below should work and send request through proxy `http://127.0.0.1:8888`, however it doesn't.

```
const axios = require("axios");
const { ProxyAgent } = require("undici");

axios
    .get(
      "http://127.0.0.1:4000",
      {
        adapter: "fetch",
        fetchOptions: {
          dispatcher: new ProxyAgent("http://127.0.0.1:8888"),
        }
      }
    )
```

### Describe the solution you'd like


After checking the source code in `lib/adapters/fetch.js` and found `fetchOptions` may need pass to `fetch()` as the second paramater.
```
export default isFetchSupported && (async (config) => {
  let {
    url,
    method,
    data,
    signal,
    cancelToken,
    timeout,
    onDownloadProgress,
    onUploadProgress,
    responseType,
    headers,
    withCredentials = 'same-origin',
    fetchOptions
  } = resolveConfig(config);

  // ...
  request = new Request(url, {
    ...fetchOptions, // <- here the fetchOptions pass to Request
    signal: composedSignal,
    method: method.toUpperCase(),
    headers: headers.normalize().toJSON(),
    body: data,
    duplex: "half",
    withCredentials
  });
  
  let response = await fetch(request); // <- not pass to fetch
```

So I pass `fetchOptions` to `fetch()`, it works. And run axios test it all passed. Also I've read the whatwg's fetch spec, I think the fetchOptions pass to `fetch()` as second param should work exactly the same as pass to `Request`.
```
  request = new Request(url, {
    signal: composedSignal,
    method: method.toUpperCase(),
    headers: headers.normalize().toJSON(),
    body: data,
    duplex: "half",
    withCredentials
  });

  let response = await fetch(request, fetchOptions);
```

However, After read the whatwg's [fetch() Spec](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-method) and the param [Request spec](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request), I know the param `dispatcher` is just a feature provided by `undici`, not in the whatwg's spec.

Not sure if this change will cause new issue or worth to be supported by axios. Somehow, I think it would be more convenient if axios can provide a way to pass the second optional param to `fetch()`.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery Vulnerability (CVE-2024-39338)
body:
### Describe the bug

Axios is vulnerable to a Server-Side Request Forgery attack caused by unexpected behaviour where requests for path relative URLS gets processed as protocol relative URLs.

This could be leveraged by an attacker to perform arbitrary requests from the server, potentially accessing internal systems or exfiltrating sensitive data.

### To Reproduce

In this vulnerable code snippet, the developer intended to invoke a path relative to the base URL, however it allows an attacker to craft a malicious protocol-relative URL which is then requested by the server. Given protocol-relative URLs are not relevant server-side as there is no protocol to be relative to, the expected result would be an error. Instead, a valid URL is produced and requested.

Example Vulnerable Code
```typescript
const axios = require('axios');

this.axios = axios.create({
  baseURL: 'https://userapi.example.com',
});

//userId = '12345';
userId = '/google.com'

this.axios.get(`/${userId}`).then(function (response) {
  console.log(`config.baseURL:  ${response.config.baseURL}`);
  console.log(`config.method:   ${response.config.method}`);
  console.log(`config.url:      ${response.config.url}`);
  console.log(`res.responseUrl: ${response.request.res.responseUrl}`);
});
```

Expected Output (Prior to axios 1.3.2):
```typescript
(node:10243) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_URL]: Invalid URL: //example.org
```

Developer might also have expected:
```yaml
config.baseURL:  https://userapi.example.com
config.method:   get
config.url:      https://userapi.example.com//www.google.com/
res.responseUrl: https://userapi.example.com//www.google.com/
```

Observed Output:
```yaml
config.baseURL:  https://userapi.example.com
config.method:   get
config.url:      //google.com
res.responseUrl: http://www.google.com/
```

This behaviour is potentially unexpected and introduces the potential for attackers to request URLs on arbitrary hosts other than the host in the base URL.

The code related to parsing and preparing the URL for server-side requests, prior to version 1.3.2, only passed one argument to the Node.js URL class.
```typescript
    const fullPath = buildFullPath(config.baseURL, config.url);
    const parsed = new URL(fullPath);
    const protocol = parsed.protocol || supportedProtocols[0];
```

Version 1.3.2 introduced `http://localhost` as a base URL for relative paths (https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/5458)
```typescript
    const fullPath = buildFullPath(config.baseURL, config.url);
    const parsed = new URL(fullPath, 'http://localhost');
    const protocol = parsed.protocol || supportedProtocols[0];
```

As protocol-relative URLs are considered to be absolute, the config.baseURL value is ignored so protocol-relative URLs are passed to the URL class without a protocol. The node.js URL class will then prepend the protocol from `'http://localhost'` to the protocol-relative URL.

For example
```typescript
> new URL('//google.com', 'https://example.org');
URL {
  href: 'https://google.com/',
  ...
}

> new URL('//google.com', 'file://example.org');
URL {
  href: 'file://google.com/',
  ...
}
```

_No response_

### Expected behavior

An error could be raised when attempting to request protocol-relative URLs server-side as unlike in a client-side browser session, there is no established protocol to be relative to.

title: isURLSameOrigin fails with URL objects due to protocol mismatch
body:
### Describe the issue

When using `isURLSameOrigin` with native Javascript URL objects, the protocols mismatch as the `resolveURL` function strips the ":"-character, while the URL-object's protocol attribute does contain it. 

`isURLSameOrigin` thus returns false if used with URL objects, even if the origins match. This now leads to issues when setting `withCredentials = true` and `withXSRFToken = false` as the XSRF token will not be submitted when using URL objects.

### Example Code

```js
// locally recreated function that mimics the relevant behavior in isURLSameOrigin
const resolveURL = function (url) {
  let href = url;
  const urlParsingNode = document.createElement('a');

  urlParsingNode.setAttribute('href', href);

  return {
    href: urlParsingNode.href,
    protocol: urlParsingNode.protocol ? urlParsingNode.protocol.replace(/:$/, '') : '',
    host: urlParsingNode.host,
    search: urlParsingNode.search ? urlParsingNode.search.replace(/^\?/, '') : '',
    hash: urlParsingNode.hash ? urlParsingNode.hash.replace(/^#/, '') : '',
    hostname: urlParsingNode.hostname,
    port: urlParsingNode.port,
    pathname: (urlParsingNode.pathname.charAt(0) === '/') ?
      urlParsingNode.pathname :
      '/' + urlParsingNode.pathname
  };
};

let originURL = resolveURL("http://www.example.com");
let requestURL = new URL("http://www.example.com");
console.log(originURL.protocol);  // > http
console.log(requestURL.protocol); // > http:
```


### Expected behavior

I do not know if this is to be disregarded as no compatibility with URL objects is explicitly proclaimed in the axios docs. My personal workaround for now is to not pass URL objects directly into axios and use strings only.

A comment in `resolveURL`  however does read "urlParsingNode provides the UrlUtils interface - http://url.spec.whatwg.org/#urlutils".
According to that spec it seems to me that the ":"-character should be included (if I am reading this correctly):
"The protocol getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)’s [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-url)’s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme), followed by U+003A (:)."

I wasted half an hour today trying to figure out why my base URL wasn't being respected, before I realized that I had spelled it `baseUrl` instead of `baseURL`. Axios silently ignored my parameter - given that Axios is liberal about accepting unknown options, I'm sure I'm not the first to trip over this and waste time on a silly ambiguity in the application of camelCase.

Any solutions here should also be applied to options such as `withXSRFToken`, ideally in an automated way so that any new options with ambiguous camelCase representations would be automatically included.

I would love if Axios simply accepted `baseUrl` as an optional spelling of `baseURL`, since Axios is already being liberal in what it accepts, and the intent is clear.

title: Request for reopen #1727 Default params serialisation behaviour incompatible with recent Tomcat versions.
body:
### Describe the bug

Request for reopening the [#1727 Default params serialisation behaviour incompatible with recent Tomcat versions.](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1727).

https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/1727#issuecomment-2244795901:

> It's unclear why it shouldn't be a default behavior - why not use standard encoding (RFC3986 / RFC1738 as qa does) as  
   expected without the need for doing workarounds?
   The problem is that one doesn't know in advance that Axios is working in such a way that might lead to unexpected bugs.

Original description
--------------------

> Summary
   Given the default params serialisation behaviour, axios out-of-the-box may fail to work with recent Tomcat versions out- 
   of-the-box.

> The problem is the way params are serialised in the absence of a custom params serialiser configuration. The code is 
   using the built-in encodeURIComponent function (good), but then proceeds to deliberately de-encode some characters. 
   In particular, it de-encodes [ and ] back to raw (problem).

> This is a problem with Tomcat because recent versions (e.g. 8.5.31+) have started being more pedantic about URI syntax, 
   and by default will reject requests that contain [ or ] in the query portion.

>  I appreciate the motive of making the URLs built by axios more human readable, and not percent-encoding characters if 
    you can get away with it. But blatant and wilful violation of RFC 3986, even if common practice for historical reasons, is a 
    problem with servers that are adopting strict-by-default behaviour.

 > Context
    axios version: v0.18.0
    Tomcat 8.5.32



reproduced on Axios 0.27.2.

title: Keep-Alive behavior is different on Node.js ≤ 18 and > 18
body:
### Describe the bug

On Node.js ≤ 18 with the http adapter, Keep-Alive is off.  
On Node.js > 18 with the http adapter, Keep-Alive is on.

The [README](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/c6cce43cd94489f655f4488c5a50ecaf781c94f2/README.md#L575) states that Keep-Alive is always off by default.

The Node.js default behavior was changed here: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/43522

It's confusing that the same axios code works differently on different Node versions.  
I'd suggest for axios to use the same Keep-Alive behavior across different Node versions.

When using the 'npm start' command to run Axios based projects with preset HTTP and HTTPS proxies, this error is triggered

	•	Impact: This vulnerability can be exploited to make unauthorized requests, potentially accessing sensitive data or systems.

I strongly recommend prioritizing the investigation and patching of this issue, as it poses a significant risk to applications using the affected versions of Axios.

title: "onUploadProgress" executes again when the request completed or failed
body:
### Describe the bug

1. "onUploadProgress" executes again when the request completed or failed. After print `[upload success]` or `[upload error]`, `[onUploadProgress]` will print agin.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e7c8c14-24a2-445f-acc6-a4b9aa87f29f)

2. `progressEvent.progress` value is incorrect.   
* If upload failed, `progressEvent.progress` increases dramatically in an instant, some times is `1`.  
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0416a72-1191-4040-a6f1-2241e222845f)
* If upload success, `progressEvent.progress` last value maybe is not `1`.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/641f7209-fb51-499b-8cdb-7b1db6250445)



### To Reproduce

_No response_

### Code snippet

```js
try {
    const res = await axios.put(url, file, {
      headers,
      onUploadProgress: progressEvent => {
        console.log('[onUploadProgress]: ', progressEvent.progress)
      },
      signal: controller?.signal,
    });
    console.log('[upload success]: ', res)
} catch(e) {
    // statements
    console.error('[upload error]: ', e);
}
```


### Expected behavior

When the request completed or failed, onUploadProgress shouldn't executes.

### Axios Version

1.7.2

### Adapter Version

_No response_

#### Summary

In the [Javascript implementation of `AxiosError`](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/core/AxiosError.js), the `status` is only attached to the `toJson`, but not in the `AxiosError` itself. However, in the [type declaration of `AxiosError`](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/4f99675fe7eae503422f932b9407242dbc1b7d55/index.d.ts#L416), there is `status?: number` field. Because of this, I have accidentally misused it for quite a while, as it is more obvious and direct than `error.response.status`.

The PR https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/5331 seems to already fix this issue, and it was even approved. But it was not merged. Can axios team merge this, or there is something else that the PR need to resolve?

title: Request.credentials breaks Cloudflare Workers since #6505
body:
### Describe the bug

#6505 addressed an issue with the fetch adapter, where it incorrectly set `withCredentials` instead of `credentials` in the `Request` object, leading to unexpected behavior.

However, fixing this issue now causes Cloudflare Workers' workerd runtime to throw `Error: The 'credentials' field on 'RequestInitializerDict' is not implemented.` as it does not support the `credentials` property (https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/2514)

### To Reproduce

Setup Axios with the fetch adapter on a Cloudflare Worker. Any request will throw.

Removing the `credentials` property in the `Request` object fixes this.
https://github.com/prianyu/axios/blob/d4ea8fb23c8fbca1bac855f81c86469c9b975e70/lib/adapters/fetch.js#L168

### Code snippet

_No response_

### Expected behavior

While I understand this is perhaps more of a Cloudflare issue than an Axios one, I hope that a solution could be implemented so we don't have to patch this manually; this wouldn't necessarily require exporting a specific build for Cloudflare Workers or adding runtime-specific checks.

A solution to this might be to change the current behavior, stop setting `credentials` to `omit` when it is not set by the user and leave it undefined. The Fetch API would the fall back to the default behavior, which is `same-origin` and not `omit` (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API/Using_Fetch#including_credentials)

Or, there could be a way to override `Request` properties set by Axios or set the `credentials` property to undefined if needed.

body:
### Describe the bug

Hello everyone,

a colleague of mine recently stumbled upon a bug, while using Axios on a Safari. It turns out, streaming with Axios and the fetch adapter is not possible on Safari.

I did some research in our code and found out, that the bug was introduced after switching from the native fetch library to Axios with fetch adapter. Nobody noticed it until recently, as it was working perfectly on Firefox and Chrome (even on MacOS).
After another bit of research, I could narrow it down to the ReadableStream response, that Axios is providing. See the attached CodeSandBox example for further details.

Why do I write it here, although it might be a bug related to the underlying Safari?
For the sake of documentation and for the sake of preventing others to fall into the same pit. And, perhaps, there is a possibility to mitigate the problem by handling the user agent in Axios directly (see workaround bit further below)?
A somewhat familiar (perhaps, the same?) issue was already reported on StackOverflow: https://stackoverflow.com/q/78713060

To anyone experiencing the same issue: There is a workaround. Detect the user agent and check for Safari. For Safari, instead of using Axios, use the native fetch library - just in case, you want to stick to Axios (like we did in our project)
For some inspiration, I created another CodeSandbox: https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/ecstatic-grass-6skn7l?workspaceId=18337018-7dab-4311-9114-b5cf242336fd

title: Breaking change in Axios 1.7.4 regarding default host in HTTP adapter
body:
### Describe the bug

This commit:
https://github.com/axios/axios/commit/6b6b605eaf73852fb2dae033f1e786155959de3a#diff-586c04c24608b86a074073c5514cc195be5c4c87ddb56da233f6d998ada4159f 
changed the code from
`const parsed = new URL(fullPath, 'http://localhost');`
to
`const parsed = new URL(fullPath, utils.hasBrowserEnv ? platform.origin : undefined);`.

This can generate an "Invalid URL" error in the URL constructor, since it expects the host to be specified.

### To Reproduce

**Please run "npm install" before trying these;** it seems that codesandbox sometimes shows up with an outdated node_modules folder?!

Not working with:
* 1.7.5: https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/sharp-dawn-3c7qk4

```
Node version: v18.20.4
Axios version: 1.7.5
node:internal/process/esm_loader:40
      internalBinding('errors').triggerUncaughtException(
                                ^
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_URL]: Invalid URL
```

Working fine with:
* 1.7.3: https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/objective-booth-98649r

```
Node version: v18.20.4
Axios version: 1.7.3
404
```

### Code snippet

```ts
const instance = new Axios({});
console.log((await instance.get('/relative')).status);
// Axios 1.7.3:  Calls http://localhost/relative
// Axios 1.7.4+: Throws "Invalid URL" from URL constructor
```

### Expected behavior

Would be be acceptable to change the code slightly like this?
```diff
- const parsed = new URL(fullPath, utils.hasBrowserEnv ? platform.origin : undefined);
+ const parsed = new URL(fullPath, utils.hasBrowserEnv ? platform.origin : 'http://localhost');
```

Then it would not be a breaking change for Node environments.
My understanding is that this wouldn't affect the CVE fix, but maybe I'm wrong.

I understand that the fallback to "localhost" is questionable, but still, removing it is a breaking change, so I suggest to delay it until version 2.0.
Your readme contains a section "Semver", which sounds like you would be using semantic versioning.

title: AxiosHeaders doesn't handle multiple headers returned via fetch adapter
body:
### Describe the bug

When using fetch adapter in node.js, axios iterates over headers by using `header.entries()` (https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/c96aa6257f5a060fedac27ae424486acd3ee705f/lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js#L104).

Headers from fetch will be in this format:
```
[
  [
    "access-control-allow-credentials",
    "true"
  ],
  [
    "access-control-allow-origin",
    ""
  ],
  [
    "connection",
    "keep-alive"
  ],
  [
    "content-length",
    "1991"
  ],
  [
    "content-type",
    "application/json; charset=utf-8"
  ],
  [
    "date",
    "Tue, 01 Oct 2024 15:49:38 GMT"
  ],
  [
    "keep-alive",
    "timeout=5"
  ],
  [
    "set-cookie",
    "test-name1=test-token1; path=/; httponly"
  ],
  [
    "set-cookie",
    "test-name2=test-token2; path=/; httponly"
  ],
  [
    "vary",
    "Origin, Accept-Encoding"
  ]
]
```

Note that there are 2 cookies set. However, axios will overwrite the first cookie with the second one.

I presume it's expecting to get cookies in an array form. But fetch adapter returns a raw list.

### To Reproduce

https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/optimistic-worker-mx8tcx?file=%2Findex.js

My output:
```
with http adapter [ 'a=x; Path=/', 'b=y; Path=/' ]
with fetch adapter b=y; Path=/
```

### Code snippet

```js
import axiosLib from "axios";

const axios1 = axiosLib.create({adapter: 'http', maxRedirects: 0, validateStatus: () => true}); 
const resp1 = await axios1.get("http://httpbin.org/cookies/set?a=x&b=y");
console.log('with http adapter', resp1.headers['set-cookie']);

const axios2 = axiosLib.create({adapter: 'fetch', maxRedirects: 0, validateStatus: () => true}); 
const resp2 = await axios2.get("http://httpbin.org/cookies/set?a=x&b=y", {
    fetchOptions: {
        redirect: 'manual'
    }
});
console.log('with fetch adapter', resp2.headers['set-cookie']);
```


### Expected behavior

Fetch adapter should reorganize headers so they are in node.js format, where repeated headers are collected.

### Axios Version

1.7.7

### Adapter Version

bundled fetch

title: Why return the string and not the JS object if we know that the responseType is JSON?
body:
https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/6841d8d18ddc71cc1bd202ffcfddb3f95622eef3/lib/adapters/xhr.js#L48

In this line, for JSON-type responses, it's returning a string. This isn't a problem because Axios' default [transformResponse](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/defaults/index.js#L100) includes a JSON.parse.

However, when implementing a custom transformResponse, I was encountering issues handling the request response. That's when I realized it's because my custom transformResponse doesn't have a JSON.parse.

title: Axios standardizes headers to be case-insensitive, which causes issues for case-sensitive APIs
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi,

I have a question regarding the capitalization of headers in Axios requests. By default, it seems that Axios capitalizes header names (e.g., "content-type" becomes "Content-Type" in some versions).

This behavior can cause issues when working with case-sensitive APIs, such as AWS API Gateway, which require headers to follow specific casing ([as noted in the AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-known-issues.html#:~:text=Header%20names%20and%20query%20parameters,back%20by%20your%20integration%20endpoint)).

I understand that this decision may follow [RFC 2616](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec4.html#sec4.2), which states that HTTP header names are case-insensitive. However, this approach can make Axios challenging to use in environments where case-sensitive headers are required.

I’ve noticed other issues opened on this topic, but they have been closed without a final solution, with the decision being to follow the specification:

Issue https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/4509
Issue https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/413

If there are other related issues, I couldn’t find them here.

Is there any way to configure Axios to send headers in a case-sensitive manner, or is there a workaround to address this issue? Any insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated!

### To Reproduce

I encountered the error while using AWS pre-signed URLs. The backend of my system generates this upload URL, and the frontend sends the file to the obtained endpoint. My API is written in .NET 8.

### Code snippet
This is an example of a manual PUT request without Axios, where headers are set to be case-sensitive:

```js

PUT /programa_29151_capitulo_9.fdx?AWSAccessKeyId=*****&Expires=1730412840&x-amz-security-token=*****&Signature=***** HTTP/1.1
accept: application/json
content-type: 
```

In comparison, here’s the same PUT request using Axios:

```js
PUT /programa_11111_capitulo_99.fdx?AWSAccessKeyId=*****&Expires=1730412968&x-amz-security-token=*****&Signature=***** HTTP/1.1
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: 
```

The only difference between these two requests is the capitalization of the content-type and accept headers, with the manual request having these headers in lowercase (content-type and accept), while Axios automatically capitalizes them (Content-Type and Accept). This is a real example I’ve encountered; the first request succeeds, but the second returns a 403 Forbidden error. I’ve hidden the other request details as they are exactly the same.

### Axios Version

1.7.7

### Node.js Version

22.2.0

### Additional Library Versions

```bash
React 18.2.0
```

Thank you!

### Describe the issue

In the latest version of axios, fetch adapter is already supported. What I want to discuss here is a scenario. I looked at the source code of fetch adapter. It determines which method to call on `Response` to get data based on the `responseType` passed in by the user.

So, if I have an api, `/api/exp`, it normally returns a `200` HTTP status code and `json` data as response's data. But in some abnormal situations, it may return a `500` HTTP status code and an `internal server error` HTML as response's data. At this time, if `res.json()` is called on the `Response` object based on the `responseType` being json, an error will be reported, prompting `SyntaxError`, and then going to `AxiosError`. This error has no response object, that is, the user cannot perceive the `500` error, but can only perceive that the request has an error.

title: Add Support for Proxy Tunneling
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Axios currently does not have native support for proxy tunneling, particularly for HTTPS requests. This limitation makes it challenging to route requests through proxies in environments that require tunneling, especially when dealing with secure servers, authenticated proxies, and complex redirect scenarios.

Proxy tunneling is critical for:

Routing HTTP and HTTPS traffic through corporate proxies.
Supporting authentication and environmental configurations (e.g., http_proxy, https_proxy, and no_proxy environment variables).
Handling redirects and secure connections in proxy scenarios.

### Describe the solution you'd like

We propose implementing native support for proxy tunneling in Axios, leveraging the widely used http-proxy-agent library. This solution has been designed to handle a variety of use cases, ensuring robust and flexible functionality.

The following cases are supported by the solution:

- Supports proxies with and without authentication
- Respects HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY environment variables
- Supports both HTTP and HTTPS servers
- Supports both HTTP and HTTPS proxies
- Handles various redirect types
- Supports exclusions via NO_PROXY environment variable

Benefits:

- Eliminates the need for external workarounds by directly integrating proxy tunneling into Axios.
- Simplifies proxy configurations for Axios users, especially in enterprise use cases.
- Enhances Axios's capabilities for routing secure traffic through proxies, making it a more versatile HTTP client.
- Handles complex scenarios, including secure proxy-server combinations and advanced redirect behaviors.

Before proceeding with a pull request, we would like feedback from the maintainers on:
- Alignment of this feature with Axios's roadmap.
- Any additional use cases or concerns to consider during implementation.

We have a solution ready that supports the described use cases using http-proxy-agent and are eager to contribute to the project.

Branch with changes : https://github.com/armandoqf/axios/tree/feature/proxying-https-requests

Thank you for your time and consideration!

title: Add generic type to response headers
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Sometimes APIs use response headers to communicate important metadata, such as rate limit information. At the moment there is no way to type what response headers we expect for a given request, which makes it hard to express/document this.

My use-case is primarily around code generation from openapi specifications, where I'd like to be able to include the declared response headers in the generated code, eg:
```yaml
          headers:
            X-RateLimit-Limit:
              "$ref": "#/components/headers/x-rate-limit-limit"
            X-RateLimit-Remaining:
              "$ref": "#/components/headers/x-rate-limit-remaining"
            X-RateLimit-Reset:
              "$ref": "#/components/headers/x-rate-limit-reset"
```
Should be expressed in output client functions like: https://github.com/mnahkies/openapi-code-generator/blob/main/integration-tests/typescript-axios/src/generated/api.github.com.yaml/client.ts#L1898-L1946

### Describe the solution you'd like

A new generic parameter added to the `AxiosResponse` and associated header types that could be used similar to this:
```typescript
type ResponseBody = {...}

type ResponseHeaders = {
  "x-rate-limit-remaining": string
  "x-rate-limit-used": string
}

function getSomeResource(): Promise<AxiosResponse<ResponseBodyType, ResponseHeaders>> {
...
}
```

Unfortunately there is already a second generic parameter on the `AxiosResponse` so care would be needed to do this in a way that was non-breaking.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I can probably workaround this on my side, either by moving away from the `AxiosResponse` type, or through an intersection type or similar, but it would be nice if `axios` made it easier to express this kind of information out of the box.

### Additional context/Screenshots

There are a couple of semi-related issues:
- https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/5967
- https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/6677

That would also be nice to see resolved.

title: Infinite loop in Axios response interceptor when rejecting an error
body:
### Describe the issue

When an API request fails (e.g., a 401 error), the error is properly intercepted in the Axios response interceptor. However, the Promise.reject() call within the interceptor causes the error to re-enter the interceptor itself. This results in an infinite loop where the error is processed repeatedly in the interceptor.

### Example Code

```js
api.interceptors.response.use(
    (response) => response,
    (error) => {
        if (error.response) {
            const errData = error.response.data;
            return Promise.reject({
                code: errData.error.code,
                type: errData.error.type,
                detail: errData.error.detail,
            });
        } 
    }
);
```


### Expected behavior

Expected Behavior:
The error should pass through the interceptor once, and the Promise.reject() should propagate the error to the calling function's catch block, without re-triggering the interceptor.

Actual Behavior:
The error enters the interceptor multiple times, causing an infinite loop. In some cases, the error.response becomes undefined in subsequent iterations, leading to unexpected behavior.

Possible Cause:
The Promise.reject() call in the interceptor is re-captured by the interceptor itself, creating a loop.

1.7.9

title: Incorrect Protocol Override in Axios Proxy Settings Leads to 400 Bad Requests
body:
### Describe the bug

Description:

An issue has been encountered with the Axios library in Node.js when using proxy settings. Currently, the code overwrites the request protocol with the proxy protocol to add ':' if it is missing (related link: [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/5097)). However, this process uses proxy.protocol as the source, which forcibly changes the original options.protocol from https to http. As a result, an https request is altered to http, leading to failed communications, and the https web server returns 400 Bad Requests.

Proposed Solution:

To resolve this issue, I propose using the original value options.protocol instead of proxy.protocol when adjusting for the presence of ':'. This would prevent unintended protocol changes and maintain the integrity of the original request. If not, I am curious if there is a design philosophy reasoning that necessitates using the same HTTPS (or HTTP for HTTP) as the target when using an HTTPS proxy.

Problem Explanation:

This request results in an unusual packet in the HTTP packet dump, where the request is actually HTTP, but the request header appears as "POST https://aaa.com/ HTTP/1.1". The correct request should be "POST aaa.com HTTP/1.1". Some proxies, such as Squid proxy, detect this issue and automatically change it back to HTTPS. However, not all proxies behave this way. Therefore, options that clearly define the communication protocol with the proxy and the protocol between the proxy and the destination are necessary for users to handle all situations.

Additional Information:

Due to these issues, Linux and Python clearly set separate proxy URLs for HTTP and HTTPS when configuring proxies. This approach ensures the use of appropriate proxies for each protocol to maintain consistency and security of requests. For example, in Python's requests library or through environment variable settings, http_proxy and https_proxy can be specified to use different proxies for HTTP and HTTPS requests, respectively. This configuration is particularly useful when different network paths are required for each protocol.

### To Reproduce

_No response_

### Code snippet

```js
    if (proxy.protocol) {
      options.protocol = proxy.protocol.includes(':') ? proxy.protocol : `${proxy.protocol}:`;
    }
```

title: Add support for mode option from Fetch in Axios (default: 'cors')
body:
#### **Description**  
Currently, Axios does not support the `mode` option from `fetch`, which can be problematic in specific scenarios, such as dealing with CORS in frontend applications. In my case, I am using a Lambda Function with CORS configured to allow any domain (`*`), but when making requests from the frontend with Axios, I encounter CORS issues.  

If it were possible to set `mode: 'no-cors'`, as in `fetch`, this issue would be resolved. However, Axios does not offer this configuration at the moment.  

#### **Context**  
- I cannot replace Axios with `fetch` due to the project’s standards.  
- I have tried alternatives such as `withCredentials: false`, proxies, and other configurations, but none of them worked.  
- The only solution that worked was using `fetch` directly with `mode: 'no-cors'`, but Axios does not offer this option.  

#### **Proposal**  
Add support for the `mode` parameter from `fetch` in Axios, allowing values such as `'no-cors'`, `'cors'`, etc.  
The default value for this configuration should be `'cors'`, ensuring that Axios’s behavior remains aligned with the conventional use of `fetch`, preventing unexpected breaks for current users.  

#### **Benefits**  
- Avoids the need to migrate parts of the code to `fetch`.  
- Makes Axios more compatible with advanced CORS configurations.  
- Maintains consistency with the default behavior of `fetch`.  
- Enhances the flexibility of the library for various frontend request scenarios.

author: lakshay-kukreja

title: Axios ignoring allowAbsoluteUrls configuration parameter
body:
### Describe the bug

Starting from Axios v1.8.0, the `allowAbsoluteUrls` attribute was introduced in the configuration to control the use of absolute URLs. (PR: https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/6795)

Currently, this parameter is being ignored in the `buildFullPath` call from the HTTP adapter.

https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/72acf759373ef4e211d5299818d19e50e08c02f8/lib/adapters/http.js#L231

This oversight means that it is still possible to make requests to absolute URLs even when the `allowAbsoluteUrls` configuration attribute is set to `false`.

### Proof of Concept:

Even though `getUri` returns a URL from `example.com`, the request is sent to `evil.com`

```javascript
> const axios = require('axios');
> axios.VERSION
'1.8.1'
> const client = axios.create({baseURL: 'http://example.com/', allowAbsoluteUrls: false});
> client.getUri({url: 'http://evil.com'});
'http://example.com/http://evil.com'
> client.get('http://evil.com');
```

### Solution:

Include the `allowAbsoluteUrls` parameter in the call to the `buildFullPath` function.

https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/72acf759373ef4e211d5299818d19e50e08c02f8/lib/adapters/http.js#L231

```javascript
const fullPath = buildFullPath(config.baseURL, config.url, config.allowAbsoluteUrls);
```

### To Reproduce

_No response_

### Code snippet

```js
const axios = require('axios');
const client = axios.create({baseURL: 'http://example.com/', allowAbsoluteUrls: false});
client.get('http://evil.com');
```

### Expected behavior

The request should be to example.com

### Axios Version

1.8.0

### Adapter Version

http

_No response_

_No response_

A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability has been identified in axios, assigned CVE-2024-39338. This vulnerability has been fixed in the 1.x branch but is still present in the 0.x branch, which is still widely used.

https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/6463

## Request

I kindly request consideration for backporting the fix for this vulnerability to the 0.x branch to ensure the security of users still relying on this version.

## Rationale

1. Security: SSRF vulnerabilities can lead to severe security issues, allowing attackers to make unauthorized requests from the server.
2. Legacy Version Support: Many projects still use the 0.x branch and may not be ready to upgrade to 1.x for various reasons.
3. Security Compliance: Backporting this fix will help projects using 0.x meet security requirements.

- CVE: CVE-2024-39338

author: rakeshy3

title: Axios Instance Documentation can do with some elaboration, as some functionality is left to be assumed
body:
### Section/Content To Improve

[The Axios Documentation](https://axios-http.com/docs/api_intro) is very clear, that you can make a request using `axios(config)`

However [The Axios Instance Documentation](https://axios-http.com/docs/instance) does not mention anywhere that you can make a request using `myAxiosInstance(config)` and the documentation simply lists the convenience methods on the Axios Instance.

### Suggested Improvement

I feel it would be an improvement to mention explicitly in the section on Axios Instance, that we can also make a request using the Axios Instance directly by calling it with a config, and not just having to invoke a convenience method on it. 

Its important to know this usage of the axios instance, as in cases where one is doing an error recovery, we may not know the original method, yet we can recover the config and do a retry, by passing the config to the instance.

e.g. `myAxiosInstance(config)`

I am using this approach in an [npm module axios-token-manager](https://github.com/mickeypuri/axios-token-manager) that I've written to do error recovery with oAuth tokens, but while reviewing it, I noticed that the axios documentation doesn't make this feature explicit.

title: Allow method-specific timeout configuration in axios.create
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently, `axios.create({ timeout })` only accepts a numeric value in milliseconds, e.g., `timeout: 3000`.

However, in real-world applications, different HTTP methods (e.g. `GET`, `POST`) often require different timeout settings.

For example, `GET` requests may need shorter timeouts while `POST` requests can afford longer ones.

### Describe the solution you'd like

While continuing to support the existing numeric value format, allow timeout to also accept an object shape like the following:

```js
axios.create({
  timeout: {
    get: 3000,
    post: 10000,
    default: 5000,
  },
});
```

This would enable more granular control, allowing each HTTP method to use a tailored timeout value. If a timeout for a specific method is not provided, the default value would be used as a fallback.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

1. Manually passing a timeout per request via `headers` or config options
   → Can result in duplicated logic across axios instances.
2. Using an interceptor to detect the request method and override timeout dynamically
   → Works, but loses the elegance and simplicity of `axios.create`-based configuration. Additionally, it becomes difficult to set a timeout for specific axios requests.

author: BangDori

title: Improve fetchOptions type definition for better autocomplete, type safety, Next.js extensions
body: ## Description: currently, the fetchOptions type in Axios is defined as Record, which limits IDE autocompletion and type safety. This issue proposes updating the type to RequestInit, the standard interface used by the Fetch API. Additionally, Next.js extends the RequestInit interface with custom options like cache and next, making this change more relevant for developers using Axios in Next.js projects. ## Why this matters: - Improved Autocompletion - using RequestInit provides developers with context-aware suggestions in IDEs. - Type Safety - ensures stricter type checking and reduces runtime errors. - Next.js Compatibility - highlights Next.js-specific extensions (next) that are compatible with the standard RequestInit. [TypeScript Declaration Merging for RequestInit in Next.js (global.d.ts)](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/types/global.d.ts) - additionally, this modification prepares Axios to accommodate future fetch options introduced by Next.js. ## Proposed Solution: - Replace the current type definition of fetchOptions with RequestInit. - Ensure compatibility with Next.js extensions by leveraging its extended interface. ## Benefits: - Aligns Axios with Fetch API standards. - Enhances developer experience, especially for Next.js users. - Provides a safer and more predictable API.

title: Using Next.js' patched fetch with Axios fetch adapter does not pass init options
body:
### Describe the bug

Minimal reproduction available [here](https://github.com/stephenliang/axios-fetch-adapter-bug).

My use case is to use the Next.js [built-in fetch caching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) implementation for Axios. To accomplish this, I create an axios instance and then adapt it to use fetch as follows:

```
const instance = axios.create({
  adapter: "fetch",
  fetchOptions: {
    cache: "force-cache", // This is a standard fetch option
    next: { revalidate: 60 }, // This is a non-standard fetch option made available by Next.js' fetch patch
  },
});
```

This works out of the box, except I need to use the [revalidate](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch#optionsnextrevalidate) feature. To do this, Next.js reads the `RequestInit` object in the fetch call, specifically:

```
fetch(resource, requestInit)
```

Without the custom `next` object being passed into fetch, next will indefinitely cache the object (since the RequestInit object comes in as `undefined`). The fetch adapter does provide for passing down `fetchOptions`, however this is spread into the Request object which erases custom objects and does not make it into actual request. 

To address, this I think the adapter needs to pass `fetchOptions` as a second parameter to `fetch` which does fix the issue but I'm unsure if there will be other impacts to doing this. I tested the following patch and it works to enable Next.js caching via Axios:

```
diff --git a/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/fetch.js b/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/fetch.js
index f871a05..1fd6cf3 100644
--- a/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/fetch.js
+++ b/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/fetch.js
@@ -167,7 +167,7 @@ export default isFetchSupported && (async (config) => {
       credentials: isCredentialsSupported ? withCredentials : undefined
     });
 
-    let response = await fetch(request);
+    let response = await fetch(request, fetchOptions);
 
     const isStreamResponse = supportsResponseStream && (responseType === 'stream' || responseType === 'response');
```

### To Reproduce

Minimal reproduction available (without Next.js) [here](https://github.com/stephenliang/axios-fetch-adapter-bug).

**Actual**:

```
Fetch called with init: undefined
Axios Response data: {
  userId: 1,
  id: 1,
  title: 'sunt aut facere repellat provident occaecati excepturi optio reprehenderit',
  body: 'quia et suscipit\n' +
    'suscipit recusandae consequuntur expedita et cum\n' +
    'reprehenderit molestiae ut ut quas totam\n' +
    'nostrum rerum est autem sunt rem eveniet architecto'
}
```

**Expected**:

```
Fetch called with init: { cache: 'force-cache', next: { revalidate: 60 } }
Axios Response data: {
  userId: 1,
  id: 1,
  title: 'sunt aut facere repellat provident occaecati excepturi optio reprehenderit',
  body: 'quia et suscipit\n' +
    'suscipit recusandae consequuntur expedita et cum\n' +
    'reprehenderit molestiae ut ut quas totam\n' +
    'nostrum rerum est autem sunt rem eveniet architecto'
}
```

### Code snippet

```js

```

### Expected behavior

next.js fetch based caching works when using the fetch adapter for axios

author: dreamforl

title: Export encode function from buildURL helper to allow code re-use
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I would like to override the Axios `paramsSerializer` with local amendments whilst re-using as much of the original Axios code as possible so that upstream changes are not lost. The problem I am facing is that the [`encode()` function](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/helpers/buildURL.js#L14) is not currently exported so that if you wanted to make use of that functionality when declaring the encode/serialize  methods of a paramsSerializer you need to either write your own `encode()` function or copy paste Axios' method into your own project.

### Describe the solution you'd like

This could be resolved by simply providing an export for the [`encode()` function](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/helpers/buildURL.js#L14)

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Currently the alternative is to vendor in the code by copy pasting the existing [`encode()` function](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.x/lib/helpers/buildURL.js#L14) into a project which comes at the risk of not receiving upstream changes.

title: Axios fails to make requests to Cloudflare-protected domains after first app launch in React Native 0.79.1
body: ### Describe the bug _Tested on iOS !_ When using Axios in a React Native app, requests to domains behind Cloudflare work the first time after a fresh build, but fail on all subsequent app launches. The error received is: AxiosError: Network Error **Additional context** This issue only seems to occur with domains that use Cloudflare. It might be a compatibility issue between Axios, React Native, and how Cloudflare handles requests or caching. Even in a completely clean React Native project with only Axios installed, this problem occurs. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a new React Native project (tested with version 0.79.1 and React 19.0.0). 2. Install Axios (tested with version 1.9.0 and 1.8.4). 3. Make a GET request to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts using Axios. 4. Run the app. The request works as expected. 5. Close and reopen the app (without rebuilding). 6. The same request now fails with a Network Error. ### Code snippet ```js axios.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts') .then((response) => { console.log('Response:', response.data); }) .catch((error) => { console.error(error); }); ``` ### Expected behavior Axios should continue to work after subsequent launches of the app, not just after a fresh build. ### Axios Version 1.9.0 ### Adapter Version _No response_ ### Browser _No response_ ### Browser Version _No response_ ### Node.js Version _No response_ ### OS iOS 18.4.1 ### Additional Library Versions ```bash React 19.0.0 React Native 0.79.1 ``` ### Additional context/Screenshots ```bash ```

title: Upgrade `formidable` to latest
body:
Lead maintainer of `formidable` here.

Any particular reason why you're using `v2`? I don't see anything that requires that version, you're using the pretty standard API - `formidable()` and then `form.parse` with a callback. On the v3 it's still the same but deprecated.

Please upgrade to latest, and prepare for `v4 `which is written in TypeScript and modern stack & APIs like Fetch/Request/Response/ReadableStream, and there is no buffering or writing to disk. You can try the `formidable@next` dist-tag. Consider supporting us, I can help with migrations if needed.

Trying to ditch people of the v1 for years, yet it has 2 million downloads and many vulnerabilities.

I'm seeing your use is in `test/unit`, but still.

title: Issue: Clarification on Axios v0.30.0 Support Status
body:
### Description:
Our project is currently using axios@0.30.0. I would like to clarify whether this version is still officially supported or has reached End of Life (EOL).

### Context:

Axios introduced the v1.x line in late 2022, and it's now at version 1.9.x.

Recently, I noticed that v0.30.0 was updated in March 2025 (reportedly a security patch for SSRF).

However, there is no clear statement on whether the 0.x branch is still maintained as part of a long-term support (LTS) strategy.

### Questions:

Is axios@0.30.0 still considered maintained by the Axios team?

If not, should we begin planning to upgrade to the latest 1.x version?

### Describe the bug When making a request with Axios, if the request fails (e.g., with a 403 Forbidden), Axios throws an error that includes the full request config—including the Authorization header—in the error object. This is the default behavior and poses a security risk, especially when error objects are logged or exposed in other ways. title: remove prepare script using husky and deprecated husky set from npm package
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi Axios contributors,

While installing axios@1.9.0 as a transitive dependency in a monorepo, I’m encountering this error:
```
npm error .git can't be found
npm error > axios@1.9.0 prepare:hooks
npm error > npx husky set .husky/commit-msg "npx commitlint --edit $1"
npm error husky - install command is DEPRECATED

```
This appears to be caused by a prepare script in package.json that looks like this:
`"scripts": {
  "prepare": "husky install && npm run prepare:hooks",
  "prepare:hooks": "npx husky set .husky/commit-msg \"npx commitlint --edit $1\""
}`

This usage of husky in a published npm package breaks installation for consumers:
	•	It assumes a .git directory exists (which is not always true in monorepos or CI)
	•	It uses deprecated Husky commands (install, set)
	•	It runs developer-only tooling during install


Please consider removing the prepare script from the published package and move hook setup to a local-only husky:init script for contributors, e.g.:

`"scripts": {
  "husky:init": "npx husky install && npx husky set .husky/commit-msg 'npx commitlint --edit $1'"
}`

### To Reproduce

1. go into a monorepo
2. install a package that wants axios 1.9.0 as  a resolution or dependencie

see above

should install as a transitive dependency in a monorepo

title: `RangeError: Invalid array length` when `data` is set to a large `Buffer`
body:
### Describe the bug

Axios triggers a `RangeError: Invalid array length` when `data` is set to a large `Buffer`

## Explanation

When axios merges configurations, it checks for empty objects:

```js
function isEmptyObject(val) {
  return val && Object.keys(val).length === 0 && Object.getPrototypeOf(val) === Object.prototype;
}
```

Calling `Object.keys` on a `Buffer` instance will try to enumerate every byte as a key. Node.js decides to die when there are more than 100-200 million keys (100-200MB byte length).

## Workaround

```ts
import axios from 'axios'

main()

async function main() {
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(1024 * 1024 * 200) // 200 MB buffer
    const arrayBuffer = buffer.buffer.slice(buffer.byteOffset, buffer.byteOffset + buffer.byteLength)
    await axios({
        method: 'POST',
        url: 'http://localhost:8080',
        data: arrayBuffer
    })
}
```

Passing `ArrayBuffer` instead of `Buffer` solves the issue, but it is not ideal as it requires additional conversion.

### To Reproduce

```ts
import axios from 'axios'

main()

async function main() {
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(1024 * 1024 * 200) // 200 MB buffer
    await axios({
        method: 'POST',
        url: 'http://localhost:8080',
        data: buffer
    })
}
```

Output:

```
~/node_modules/axios/lib/utils.js:134
  return val && Object.keys(val).length === 0 && Object.getPrototypeOf(val) === Object.prototype;
                       ^

RangeError: Invalid array length
    at Function.keys (<anonymous>)
    at Object.isEmptyObject (~/node_modules/axios/lib/utils.js:134:24)
    at getMergedValue (~/node_modules/axios/lib/core/mergeConfig.js:21:22)
    at valueFromConfig2 (~/node_modules/axios/lib/core/mergeConfig.js:43:14)
    at computeConfigValue (~/node_modules/axios/lib/core/mergeConfig.js:98:23)
    at Object.forEach (~/node_modules/axios/lib/utils.js:281:10)
    at mergeConfig (~/node_modules/axios/lib/core/mergeConfig.js:96:9)
    at Axios.request (~/node_modules/axios/lib/core/Axios.js:41:12)
    at wrap (~/node_modules/axios/lib/helpers/bind.js:5:15)
    at main (~/src/axios.ts:7:11)

Node.js v20.18.3
```

### Code snippet

```js

```

### Expected behavior

Since `Buffer` is common, e.g. the default return types of `readFile` or `readFileSync` are Buffers, naively trying to upload a large file in Node.js will trigger this error.

When `typeof Buffer !== 'undefined'`, `axios` should detect and work with it properly during configuration merging.

title: Discrepancies between types from index.d.cts and index.d.ts
body:
### Describe the bug

As of v1.10.0, the following discrepancies exist between the types from https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.cts (CJS) and https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.ts (ESM), making their corresponding types incompatible:

## `AxiosHeaders` class

ESM class `AxiosHeaders` [contains](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.ts#L77) a `getSetCookie(): string[];` but is missing from its CJS [counterpart](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.cts#L19-L81).

## `AxiosHeaderMatcher` type

ESM type `AxiosHeaderMatcher` is [defined as](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.ts#L12):

```typescript
type AxiosHeaderMatcher =
  | string
  | RegExp
  | ((this: AxiosHeaders, value: string, name: string) => boolean);
```

while its CJS counterpart is [defined as](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.cts#L9):
```typescript
type AxiosHeaderMatcher = (
  this: AxiosHeaders,
  value: string,
  name: string,
  headers: RawAxiosHeaders
) => boolean;
```

## `InternalAxiosRequestConfig` interface

ESM interface `InternalAxiosRequestConfig` is [defined as](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.ts#L370-L372)
```typescript
export interface InternalAxiosRequestConfig<D = any> extends AxiosRequestConfig<D> {
  headers: AxiosRequestHeaders;
}
```

while its CJS [counterpart](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.cts#L427-L429) is missing the generic type param for `AxiosRequestConfig`:
```typescript
interface InternalAxiosRequestConfig<D = any> extends AxiosRequestConfig {
  headers: AxiosRequestHeaders;
}
```

## `AxiosError` class
ESM class `AxiosError` [contains](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.ts#L422-L429) a static method `from`:
```typescript
static from<T = unknown, D = any>(
  error: Error | unknown,
  code?: string,
  config?: InternalAxiosRequestConfig<D>,
  request?: any,
  response?: AxiosResponse<T, D>,
  customProps?: object,
): AxiosError<T, D>;
```
while its CJS [counterpart](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.cts#L83-L112) has no such method.

## `AxiosStatic` interface
ESM interface `AxiosStatic` [contains](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.ts#L549-L568) a `mergeConfig` method:
```typescript
export function mergeConfig<D = any>(config1: AxiosRequestConfig<D>, config2: AxiosRequestConfig<D>): AxiosRequestConfig<D>;

//...

export interface AxiosStatic extends AxiosInstance {
  // ...
  mergeConfig: typeof mergeConfig;
}
```

while its CJS [counterpart](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/v1.10.0/index.d.cts#L529-L545) does not contain such a method.

author: powerdev9

title: Improve network error reporting by exposing underlying error messages and codes
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently Axios collapses all low‑level failures into a generic Network Error (or Request aborted), hiding the real cause—whether it’s a TLS handshake failure, DNS lookup error, connection refused, or other issue. This makes debugging extremely difficult, especially in React Native (XHR adapter) and Node.js (HTTP adapter) environments.

What happens today:

- **Browser/XHR:** request.onerror always rejects with new AxiosError('Network Error', ERR_NETWORK), discarding any information in the error event.
- **Node/HTTP:** req.on('error') rejects with AxiosError.from(err…), but doesn’t surface err.code (e.g. UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE) or the original err.message.
- Why it matters:

Developers spend “light‑years” debugging generic errors instead of seeing the real SSL/TLS or connectivity issue.
It’s impossible to programmatically handle specific network error codes (retries on timeouts, certificate pinning prompts, fallback logic, etc.).

### Describe the solution you'd like

1. **XHR adapter**

   * In `request.onabort`, wrap and reject with an `AxiosError` whose `.message` and `.event` include the underlying `event.message`.
   * In `request.onerror`, pull `event.message` (if any) into the `AxiosError` and attach `error.event = event`.

2. **HTTP adapter**

   * In `req.on('error')`, build the rejection error so that:

     ```js
     const msg = err.code
       ? `${err.code} – ${err.message}`
       : err.message || 'Network Error';
     const axiosErr = AxiosError.from(err, null, config, req);
     axiosErr.message = msg;
     axiosErr.code = err.code;
     axiosErr.originalError = err;
     reject(axiosErr);
     ```
   * This surfaces Node.js error codes (e.g. `ECONNREFUSED`, `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`) and the full message.

**Benefits:**

* Immediate visibility into SSL certificate validation failures, DNS issues, CORS errors, etc.
* Enables consumers to inspect `error.code`, `error.event`, or `error.originalError` for richer error handling.
* Backward‑compatible: existing code that checks only `error.message` or `error.code` still works, but now gets more detail.

**Next steps / How to help:**

* Feedback on the approach before writing tests.
* Volunteers to help add unit tests simulating XHR and Node TLS errors.
* Documentation updates to highlight the new fields (`error.event`, `error.originalError`).

Let’s give Axios users the clarity they deserve!


### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

title: Axios next
body:
Over the last 6 months, I have been giving a large amount of thought to Axios and how we can potentially solve many legacy issues we have, as well as start working towards a more modern and sustainable DX.

Based on this, building a completely new version of Axios with all the latest standards and best practices in mind is the best way to move forward. We will continue to maintain v1 for the foreseeable future; however, it will undergo a complete rewrite with a focus on modern JavaScript features, improved performance, and a better developer experience.

**Concepts**

- **Modular Architecture**: Axios next will be built with a modular architecture, allowing developers to include only the parts they need, reducing bundle size and improving performance.
- **TypeScript First**: The new version will be developed with TypeScript from the ground up, ensuring better type safety and developer tooling support.
- **Improved Interceptors**: We will enhance the interceptor system to be more flexible and powerful, allowing for easier manipulation of requests and responses.
- **Better Error Handling**: Axios next will introduce a more robust error handling system, making it easier to catch and handle errors consistently.
- **Enhanced Documentation**: We will provide comprehensive and clear documentation, including examples and tutorials to help developers get started quickly and effectively.

**Plan/Timeline**

- **Q4 2025**: Initial planning and architecture design. Set up the project structure and development environment.
- **Q1 2026**: Begin development of core features, including modular architecture and TypeScript integration.
- **Q2 2026**: Implement improved interceptors and error handling systems. Start writing documentation and examples.
- **Q3 2026**: Focus on performance optimizations and finalizing the API. Begin alpha testing with a select group of community members.
- **Q4 2026**: Launch beta version of Axios next. Gather feedback from the community and make necessary adjustments.
- **Q1 2027**: Finalize the release candidate based on beta feedback.
- **Q2 2027**: Official release of Axios next. Continue to maintain v1 for legacy support while encouraging migration to next.

This plan is ambitious, but I believe it is necessary to ensure that Axios remains a relevant and powerful tool for developers in the years to come. The given timeline may change, but this is a rough indication. I am excited about the possibilities that Axios next will bring and look forward to collaborating with the community throughout this process. Please feel free to leave your feedback or comments on this post.

title: Axios issue and PR cleanup
body:
Axios has a very large backlog of both issues and PR's that have been sitting around for a very long period of time this causes a lot of noise for anyone trying to interact with the repo. I am going to comb through a multitude of issues, closing anything that is stale and older than about a year. I will handle the following types of issues as follows:

Bugs:
For any bug that is stale I will close the issue and ask that if this still occurs we create a new issue based on the latest version of Axios.

Features:
I will close any feature that is stale, however if this is something I can see us adding to Axios at a future point I will add it to a roadmap.

PR:
If any of these are to stale to merge i will ask for the author to re-open based on the latest version. If this is a un-feasible change i will close it and mark it as such.

This should enable a cleaner and less noisy experience with Axios in general and hopefully help us with more quality contribution and easier to manage issues and PR's

title: Axios fetch adapter: Missing boundary when Content-Type is set manually with FormData
body:
### Describe the bug

When using the fetch adapter with FormData, if I manually set the Content-Type: multipart/form-data header, Axios does not include the boundary, which causes the server to reject the request.

This is inconsistent with native fetch, which automatically appends the boundary even if the header is set manually.

### To Reproduce

`import axios from "axios";

const http = axios.create({ adapter: "fetch" });

const form = new FormData();
form.append("file", new Blob(["test content"], { type: "text/plain" }), "test.txt");

// Manually set Content-Type
const { data } = await http.post("/upload", form, {
  headers: { "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data" },
});
`

### Code snippet

```js
Content-Type: multipart/form-data   <-- missing boundary
```

### Expected behavior

Axios should either:

- Automatically append the correct boundary to multipart/form-data, or
- Warn developers not to override Content-Type when using FormData.



### Axios Version

1.12.0

### Adapter Version

fetch

### Browser

Chrome 139.0.7258.67

_No response_

22.17.1
